review_text:
I should start by mentioning that I first heard about this game through a YouTuber named "TheMysteriousMrEnter." He's used music from this game in his videos and credited the songs from the OST. I looked up the game itself, and I initially thought this was going to be an homage to JRPG's from the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis era, like Undertale. The game itself makes a small joke about that, pretending to start up a turn-based battle, but then they just move forward.

I will say, first and foremost, that I enjoy the narrative and presentation. The graphics, while simple, use a lot of muted colors and a low resolution to create a realistic atmosphere; the music is beautiful, especially the main theme, "Everything's Alright."

The premise is an interesting idea, where two scientists, Eva Rosalene and Neil Watts, work together to alter a dying man's memories, to fulfill his wish to travel to the moon. As the game goes on, you see what sparked this motive, and the life he and his family had over the years. There's also several unexpected turns that leave you guessing how this man dealt with tragedies and grief that occurred in his life, and what the scientists will do to achieve their mission. I was about to HATE the ending when the female scientist went off by herself to alter the man's memories in a certain way, because it meant the man would completely forget about a huge chuck of his life, one that he should be able to remember; but then I see how she replaced his memories, and the payoff at the end, as well as her actions, felt justified.

So what's my problem here? The gameplay, or lack thereof. As I mentioned, this is not an RPG like I was expecting; it's an adventure game where you solve puzzles and use the man's memories to, in a sense, travel through time. You can't go all the way back to his earliest memories in one "memory hop", you have to perform numerous backwards hops over the course of the man's life. You do this by finding a "memento", a concrete object from the man's memories, which have to be activated using 5 "memory links", other objects and small details in the background found by combing over a contained environment. When you take the memory links to the memento and activate it, you solve a simple puzzle, which is flipping all the tiles to form a picture of the memento. You have to do this process at least 7 or 8 times, while watching the story play out; it gets just as repetitive, and sometimes confusing, as finding a certain number of magical glowey things in a 3D platformer to unlock the next stage. Once you've done this process enough times, you have to link the mementos together in a chain so the scientists can go back to the man's earliest memory, alter it, and set a butterfly effect into motion, thus fulfilling his wish.

But that's just Act 1! The second act of the game involve the scientists finding alternative methods to go all the way back to the man's earliest memory, which they can't immediately access; the third act of the game is watching the earliest memory, followed by a disjointed climax where Dr. Watts has to chase down Dr. Rosalene who goes off on her own to alter the man's memories, without explaining the plan to him. Throughout all of this, there's 5 or 6 detours that the scientists have to take to solve problems, and the solutions they come up with are sometimes nonsensical. 

Again, I like the narrative of this game, but that's just it: this story doesn't work as a video game! The gameplay, while interactive, is so minimal, that a single playthrough just becomes a tour through set pieces, automatically moving forward in a straight line at a certain pace. The most freedom you get is talking to NPC's and looking at certain objects in the contained environments. This should've been a graphic novel or an animated movie, because it feels disjointed and bogged down as an interactive medium.

Even the two free "minisodes" are just really short epilogues where you're wandering back and forth through the building where the scientists work.

Speaking of them, another problem I have is the two scientists as characters. Dr. Rosaline and Dr. Watts spend the WHOLE GAME constantly bickering and trying to one-up each other over the course of their mission. It's fine if they're not best of friends, or they disagree on how to go about the mission, but they don't even act professional or civil with each other; it's just mindless fighting and word games between these two. They obviously need to be there as protagonists, and they shouldn't just be blank slates, but when I follow a pair of grown adults acting like children fighting on the playground, and I have to watch the story unfold from their perspective, it ends up bringing down what's otherwise a beautiful story about seeing a dying man's dreams come true. Imagine going to a large, elaborate wedding, and you have to sit next to your two friends who spend the whole ceremony yelling at each other in the back of the venue; that's my metaphor for the scientists in this game.

So I unfortunately can't recommend this game. Watch a "Let's Play" on YouTube to experience the story, and then buy the soundtrack on the developers' Band Camp page, instead. You'll actually get more out of it that way.

while simple , use a lot of muted colors and a low resolution to create a realistic atmosphere the music is beautiful , especially the main theme , everything ' s alright . the premise is an interesting idea , where two scientists , eva rosalene and neil watts , work together to alter a dying man ' s memories , to fulfill his wish to travel to the moon . as the game goes on , you see what sparked this motive , and the life he and his family had over the years . there ' s also several unexpected turns that leave you guessing how this man dealt with tragedies and grief that occurred in his life , and what the scientists will do to achieve their mission . i was about to hate the ending when the female scientist went off by herself to alter the man ' s memories in a certain way , because it meant the man would completely forget about a huge chuck of his life , one that he should be able to remember but then i see how she replaced his memories , and the payoff at the end , as well as her actions , felt justified . so what ' s my problem here ? the gameplay , or lack thereof . as i mentioned , this is not an rpg like i was expecting it ' s an adventure game where you solve puzzles and use the man ' s memories to , in a sense , travel through time . you can ' t go all the way back to his earliest memories in one memory hop , you have to perform numerous backwards hops over the course of the man ' s life . you do this by finding a memento , a concrete object from the man ' s memories , which have to be activated using 5 memory links , other objects and small details in the background found by combing over a contained environment . when you take the memory links to the memento and activate it , you solve a simple puzzle , which is flipping all the tiles to form a picture of the memento . you have to do this process at least 7 or 8 times , while watching the story play out it gets just as repetitive , and sometimes confusing , as finding a certain number of magical glowey things in a 3d platformer to unlock the next stage . once you ' ve done this process enough times , you have to link the mementos together in a chain so the scientists can go back to the man ' s earliest memory , alter it , and set a butterfly effect into motion , thus fulfilling his wish . but that ' s just act 1 ! the second act of the game involve the scientists finding alternative methods to go all the way back to the man ' s earliest memory , which they can ' t immediately access the third act of the game is watching the earliest memory , followed by a disjointed climax where dr . watts has to chase down dr . rosalene who goes off on her own to alter the man ' s memories , without explaining the plan to him . throughout all of this , there ' s 5 or 6 detours that the scientists have to take to solve problems , and the solutions they come up with are sometimes nonsensical . again , i like the narrative of this game , but that ' s just it this story doesn ' t work as a video game ! the gameplay , while interactive , is so minimal , that a single playthrough just becomes a tour through set pieces , automatically moving forward in a straight line at a certain pace . the most freedom you get is talking to npc ' s and looking at certain objects in the contained environments . this should ' ve been a graphic novel or an animated movie , because it feels disjointed and bogged down as an interactive medium . even the two free minisodes are just really short epilogues where you ' re wandering back and forth through the building where the scientists work . speaking of them , another problem i have is the two scientists as characters . dr . rosaline and dr . watts spend the whole game constantly bickering and trying to one-up each other over the course of their mission . it ' s fine if they ' re not best of friends , or they disagree on how to go about the mission , but they don ' t even act professional or civil with each other it ' s just mindless fighting and word games between these two . they obviously need to be there as protagonists , and they shouldn ' t just be blank slates , but when i follow a pair of grown adults acting like children fighting on the playground , and i have to watch the story unfold from their perspective , it ends up bringing down what ' s otherwise a beautiful story about seeing a dying man ' s dreams come true . imagine going to a large , elaborate wedding , and you have to sit next to your two friends who spend the whole ceremony yelling at each other in the back of the venue that ' s my metaphor for the scientists in this game . so i unfortunately can ' t recommend this game . watch a let ' s play on youtube to experience the story , and then buy the soundtrack on the developers ' band camp page , instead . you ' ll actually get more out of it that way .

review_text:
The Callisto Protocol is to Dead Space as Lord's of the Fallen is to Dark Souls.

My wife’s boyfriend on the other hand says the Callisto Protocol is to Dead Space what Back 4 Blood was to Left 4 Dead.

It feels kind of The-Order-1886-ly in that it truly looks amazing but the game itself is lacking. That said, while the combat does get kind of janky at times, the atmosphere does feel tense and scary. To me it's a great example of like, sure, graphics in a game aren't everything... but they sure as sh*t can be something. What's funny is that this feels exactly like when Evil Within came out. A great survival horror developer branches out and makes their own IP complete with janky combat and difficulty spikes. And like with Evil Within, I'm actually enjoying Callisto. It won't be winning any game of the year awards, but it's still neat. I have a feeling this game will be appreciated more as time goes on, just like the evil within 1, people had expectations that didn't live up, but maybe later people will appreciate it for what it is, because this feels unique and fresh in gameplay and art direction and tone... if you like condemned, escape from butcher bay, dead space, the evil within then this is a must.

This game released at the best time for me. l needed a break from 40+ hr RPGS and open world games for a while. I found the game really enjoyable and damn the graphics look amazing to compliment the bone crushing melee combat. It’s not for everyone though, survival horror never is. It is extremely engrossing, the atmosphere and tone is amazing, the world is insanely detailed and the sound design is - excuse my French - fu*king spectacular. I had been waiting a long time for this game to drop and I was extremely satisfied. A linear, single player, story driven experience arriving just in time during a season bogged down by online competitive shooters. It's a breath of fresh air. What surprised me the most is it's an actual FINISHED game.

I think graphically and visually it’s a total knockout. Literally one of the best looking games I have ever seen ever in my entire life. Now, I'm someone who hates cinematic games and walking simulators and the game does have a bunch of that, but in the end I still enjoyed it. I think the most divisive thing is how clunky it feels. The combat as janky as it was, still felt satisfying and fun most of the time and the big complaint "melee focused combat" is totally false and overblown by the way. You'll be throwing enemies at spikes, launching items at them, secondary fire explosisions, power shot gun. Its a big mix. If you only melee it's honestly on you. They post added more melee finishers too, and they are intensely awesome ways to finish fights.

The Callisto Protocol is a solid 8/10 game in my opinion. Brilliant setting, graphically beautiful, sounds great I finished it and overall enjoyed the world and story. If you enjoy Dead Space I would say to at least play it through once if you get the opportunity. Don’t listen to people who are so fanatical about horror games that they don’t want you to have a good time. They want you to be in constant fear and stressed out. That’s not fun. It’s a game for people to enjoy, as video games are supposed to be not to cause stress or the feeling of having heart attack every time you play, f*ck that. It feels almost like an old school survival horror which I like, but with some modern jank too (walking sim parts).

Big picture? Game is flawed but way better than people give it credit for. Is it on the level of DS remake or RE4? No. Is it still a solid visually stunning action horror game with replay value? Absolutely. If you go in to the game to play a Dead Space game the way every other idiot does then no it’s not worth it. If you go in to play the Callisto Protocol it’s a hell of a ride. People just can’t get over that the game is not called Dead Space and it doesn’t play like Dead Space. The game is great for what it is. This isn't some epic narrative driven movie RPG. It's a blood and guts killfest. And I loved it for that, end of story. If you want a short and mostly fun (but janky) scifi horror game to get some of the DS vibes back I'd recommend it. 

Would play it again to get some more eye candy. And by eye candy, I mean the Asian chick from The Boys, of course.

8/10

review_text:
This game has seemingly infinite potential and, in the state it's in, is worlds of fun. It's a 4 out of 5 and could be a 5 out of 5 with some tweaks and additional content.

I've been looking for an NHL Hitz-style game for what seems like forever, but everything I've played has fallen short. One problem this game has (like literally every other hockey game in history) is cheap goals. Far too many times is the cpu opponent able to seemingly score at will. It forces you to place as tight defensively as possible, which, to an extent, is good, it just shouldn't be because the cpu can score from anywhere on the ice whenever it wants or is needed. It's a gripe I would have with any game, so it's not unique to Tape to Tape.

The customization of uniforms is nice, but quickly falls flat when you realize it's only one template that you get to recolor, rather than having a variety of designs and styles. It's something that could possibly be added in the future, which I hope is the case.

I've seen the development road map for the game and it looks like there will eventually be a season mode. That's great, but how about a franchise mode? How about a bit of depth? How about significantly expanded customization for both uniforms and created players? These are all things I'd love to see.

Tape to Tape has the potential to be a game that becomes a cult classic, something people look back on and say, "Yeah, I miss playing that game, it was so much fun," but in order to get there, there needs to be a lot more content and a lot more options and functionality. Definitely a great place to start, though. Fingers crossed.

review_text:
Despite playing for 69 minutes (appropriate time to review this) I feel I've experienced almost all of what the game has to offer, and that's not necessarily a bad thing! There's a simplicity to it that you could enjoy.

The Good:

1. There's a strategy to it of course, you could maybe run in with just a hand full of one class but given the later levels, putting your mind to the test in terms of class selections, character placements, it's pretty battling in terms of tactics.

2. It's... weird, weird in by there are little choices in the beginning of every level that have the most outlandish writing, it's goofy and offers a reward depending on the choice.

3. Classes and enemy designs and the such are like an amalgamation of separate games and movies to somewhat of a little extent, but at one point during gameplay, it becomes Lovecraftian, adding a welcome spice to your playthrough.

The Bad:

1. It of course gets repetitive at some point, I have yet to feel that after 69 minutes but I could feel it'll happen soon enough, but given the mechanics of the gameplay, maybe it could be pushed through.

2. The game isn't exactly fleshed out, meaning that you learn almost all of the controls, like I said, in the beginning of the game, and from that point on it's dependent on difficulty and RNG in terms of enemy spawns.

Conclusion:

I'd for sure recommend it, it's goofy, doesn't take itself too seriously, and straight to the point. With the price it is at, most definitely worth it, on top of that, the game is still being worked on, improved, and added on by the devs, so more madness to come.

review_text:
Battle Nations is a fairly good game, if you can look past the bugs it has. Some of which have been in the game for months. Despite the fact that there are units you can only buy with premium currency (nanopods), I wouldn't really call it pay2win, since you can still beat them with normal units, albeit with more difficulty. There is also a possibility to gain nanopods for free during the boss strikes once a month, so there is that as well. It's not exactly unfair. If you are familiar with these kind of games, you won't mind the long upgrade and build times, since you will be used to them from other games in that genre. A levelsystem for your base that doesn't need forever to fill up also keeps you motivated to keep at it and expand your base to grow even stronger. Which is good, given the fact that you will need to level up to unlock new buildings, ressources and units.

Pros:

- Very likable and humorous characters and storyline. A very good mix between seriousness and comedy.
- A small, but still nice Soundtrack. Some effort went into creating those tracks.
- An easy to understand combat system that still is a lot of fun despite its simplicity.
- Regular events such as Boss Strikes, which offer great rewards for everyone participating.
- Company behind the game appears to be very involved with its community.

Cons:

- Very unstable game that keeps crashing. Very annoying.
- An interface that obviously wasn't created with PCs in mind. You will see immediately that this game was intended to be a mobile game first, before getting ported to a PC version.
- The PvP system, albeit present, isn't really worth mentioning. I hardly ever saw anyone use it. Technically, the occupation feature could be considered PvP as well, but no one ever does it to fight each other, but rather to help the occupying player to get some resources. I don't find this to be really THAT bad, but for people who look for a game in which they can bash and farm weaker players all day, this would certainly be a downer.
- You literally have to grow a big friends list and help them regularily if you don't want to wait forever to have enough resources to build something. While this, in it's principe, is good, it quickly becomes tiresome to do this every day.
- Finding a guild takes some effort, because the bad interface doesn't allow for an easy search of the existing ones. Since a lot of small and/or inactive guilds exist, finding an actual working one is quite bothersome. Took me several forum posts and tryouts to find one that wasn't utter crap.
- I find the unit info screen to be lacking. I often tried to find information there, but had to realize that it just wasn't there. And if it was, I haven't found it to this very day. Even such crucial things such as "can attack air" or "can't attack air" aren't showed there, not to mention that the unit info screen crashes 7 out of 10 times upon opening it.

tl;dr:

good game, but needs improvement in terms of bugs and interface. The world, characters, story and gameplay are good and  probably the only reason I am still sticking around, despite the bugs. It definitely has more charm than most games in this genre, now all it needs is to stop crashing all the time.

Uff.. at first I gave this game a recommendation... but after playing for longer it jsut became unbearable.

The Good:

+ It's a great game with a superb atmosphere and good story.
+ Bizarre, confusing and not always easy to follow plotlines.
+ Graphics and Sounds are fitting.
+ Fully adjustable difficulty settings let you customize the game so the most annoying parts (like hunger and thirst) that dont really add to the game can be minimized.

The Bad:

- Dialogues arent voiced. Which makes for a tedious read.
- Gameplay is.. well crap. Gameplay consists only of running from A to B and talking to people. Rare (and annoying) fights happen... as well as other elements that are in the game but are either so rare or entirely unrelevant to the game (autopsies, lockpicking....)
- Layout of the Town is atrocious. When your gameplay consists of running from A to B you should make the level design accordingly. its a pain running around with tiny fences blocking your path, forcing you to take huge detours nonstop.

BUT .... Fazit:
This is what breaks the game for me:
All the atmosphere is useless if you create a game where the player has to literally SPRINT every second to have a glimmer of hope to get MOST things done. even on a second playthrough I couldnt do it.

Even worse: 
Dialogue Options have NO impact on anything. You will notice this on a second playthrough: it doesnt matter if you are nice or an asshole, ask them about A or B: The response is the EXACT same thing.

This and some other bad design choices made me abandoned the game

review_text:
"Mom, can we stop for Dead Space?"
"No sweetie, we have Dead Space at home."

I really wanted to like this game, and after finishing the main story (still deciding if I'll go back for DLC) the best thing I can say about it is that I guess it was OK for $25 CAD for the Deluxe edition on sale. 

I had no issues with the performance all the way through, and the combat was mostly enjoyable, but WOW was the level design atrocious, almost all throughout. Your character's default walking speed was comically slow to begin with, but that's ok, because you spend most of your time crawling, sidling, and wading through forced slow-movement sections that, if used smartly, could have ramped up the tension, but there were entire sections of crawling through a duct, walking 8 feet, crawling through another duct, walking 10 feet, slowly squeezing through a narrow gap, walking 8 feet, and on, and on, and on. 

Then there was the unending "stealth" section where the game beats into you that the enemies are blind but have excellent hearing so you need to be silent. Turns out that excellent hearing doesn't apply when you're 6 feet away and perform a "stealth" kill wherein you loudly grunt while ramming a shiv through an enemy's skull, toss the body to the side, then stomp on it for the loot. But boy, if you stand up from a crouch, even for a second, get ready for every enemy in the room to come for you.

I am a big fan of stealth games like Hitman, Sniper Elite, Metal Gear, and Tom Clancy to name a few. I bought this game because a friend told me it was good but oh god. I wasted money on buying the whole franchise on sale. There are so many jarring issues with this game that makes this a grueling experience. I rarely ever write reviews for games but this game just doesn't sit right with me.

- Cameras and guards have ridiculous lines of sight and they see you almost immediately 
- When spotted everybody hive minds to you at once and will try to shoot at you from 200 feet away through multiple buildings
- Main objectives are pickups that are on or near targets making sniping more pointless than it already is 
- So many unnecessary additions that just make the gameplay more complex instead of unique
- You will have to spend copious amounts of hours to unlock skills to make the game "better"
- It's not very well optimized, some areas I will run at a smooth 60 FPS then I just look 2 feet to my left and I'm at 30 FPS
- The save system is possibly the worst feature, with no manual saving and the game barely autosaves every 30 minutes, and not even after completing an objective!
- The skill system is the same with weapon unlocks
- The main character's voice acting is terrible and has no emotion nor does it fit his character
- People can literally spawn right next you
- Despite having futuristic gear you will almost immediately freeze to death in water and you will die in 2 hits
- The climbing system is just abhorrent with you being only able to climb on extremely specific surfaces even if i should clearly and logically be able to climb on something
- The interaction button doesn't always work and will require you to press it multiple times for it to work
- Every feature in this is just stolen from other games that are actually good and the features that aren't from other games are unnecessary and are terrible
- Melee and your pistol will be used way more than your sniper rifle ever will
- Why are grenades bound to F and why are there even grenades in the first place!?!
- There are random traps you can pick up that you'll never use
- The only good and more unique feature is interrogating enemies but that's still nothing new
- The controls are just not great
- You are forced to watch a cutscene that you've already scene if you re-enter and mission and you can't skip it
- If you go to the developer's (CI Games) other games on Steam 90% of them have bad reviews, in fact, there are more games in this specific franchise with bad reviews then there are good ones!
- Only 44% of people have even completed the first mission
- The sniping mechanics are not difficult at all and it basically tells you where to aim and you can line up a shot in 2 seconds flat
- The developers are aware of the bad save system and don't care or plan to change/fix it!
- Despite being one of the best snipers in the world you can hold your breath for ONLY 4 SECONDS!!!! WHY!?

From taking down hordes of enemies (I am not joking) to solving complex puzzles, this game provides you with a good range of challenges. However, in the PC version, the keys are spread out between a mouse, the left side of the keyboard, and the number keys, and while the formatting is nice, it makes it very annoying if your controller is not made for connecting to PC. As such, I would not recommend this for anyone who is used to controller games but does not have the capacity to use one.

review_text: I bought this game a few years ago, but since I have been going through my Steam library trying to play my short, story line Indie games, I thought I would give this a try. At first I read the other reviews talking about how wonderful this game is and how the dialogue is phenomenal and will make you sob playing it. I can assure you that this is not true. There are few instructions of how to move around in the game, meaning that it took me until nearly the end of the game before I realized I could use arrow keys to move the main characters rather than pointing and clicking the location for them to travel. The actual minigames within this are incredibly easy, such as finding items as mementos to travel through the man's memories, and this puzzle that you have to complete before travelling. It propels you along a linear story line with very little help from the player besides moving around through the map. The pixel graphics are good for their type and age, but when it comes to the dialogue, it is horrific. The dialogue appears in text boxes, and sometimes the dialogue wasn't fully in the box to be able to read. Through about half the game there was a way to make the dialogue automatically appear rather than scroll as the character is speaking, but then this option was disabled, meaning you have to watch every useless strand of dialogue appear on the screen. The dialogue itself, while it has previously been praised, is about on par with a Wattpad fanfiction writer, and uses many colloquialisms in the speech (and sometimes not even colloquialisms, but just slang that you may only use in text messages or bad stories on the internet). While I admit that the plot is a tear-jerker, this is simply because they throw additional plot twists in here almost as if it is a drama on TV, not because it makes sense in the given context. Pretty much, the story only makes you cry because they just keep adding sadness for the sake of sadness. Much of the dialogue doesn't make sense realistically, and the humor is awful. The characters aren't fleshed out at all, and while the symbolism is sweet and this contains an adorable love story, it isn't worth the 3-4 hours spent playing the game to achieve the mediocre ending. I will say, one perk is that there is a lovely violin soundtrack that is quite peaceful to listen to. Otherwise, I wouldn't bother spending the money to purchase this.

Based on my limited research it seems that the devs have already added/fixed some features/issues in the game (i.e. being able to chat with people in your party before loading into a level, adding a slide release input for guns, etc).

I'm having fun with this game so far.  I'm not having too much trouble finding matches due to crossplay support - it seems that most of the players that I'm encountering are playing on the Meta Quest 2.

Overall I like this game.  I find it fun.  I really like co-op shooters, and playing one in VR is all the more interesting IMO.  The game is far from perfect right now, but it also just came out just one month ago.  I, for one, am optimistic and eagerly awaiting the new incoming content that the devs plan to release for this game in its upcoming "seasons".

review_text: Felt like a Dead Space fangame. The central enemy gimmick to replace "cut off their limbs" is "kill them before they merge" which is trivial to do so merging basically never happens (I think the stat screen at the end of my play-through showed 15 merged enemies over an eight-hour playthrough and hundreds of things killed). It has a stomp like Dead Space which is pointless as dead enemies do not give loot and your melee opens crates fine. There's no equivalent to the kinesis or stasis modules so combat is very by-rote and won't change from the start of the game with the handgun to the end of the game where you will in all likelihood still be using the handgun. The plot is a fairly standard post-apocalyptic time-travel story that doesn't really go anywhere interesting. The atmosphere is the saving grace. Get it on sale.

review_text:
While I wouldn't call myself a Left 4 Dead fan, I am very passionate about this game and the sequel, even to the point where I've played all of Back 4 Blood for some reason. In general, Left 4 Dead 2 is one of my favourite video games of all time, would be my favourite zombie (or infected, whatever) game if it weren't for plants vs zombies garden warfare, yes I am being serious. I love almost everything about this duology, from the gunplay to the artwork to the story to the mods to even the menu design, it is all impressive. Not my favourite duology because of reasons mentioned two sentences ago, but still very much up there. Here's the thing however, one thing I have intentionally excluded from the list is the characters, which are famously what makes L4D so good in so many of the playerbase's eyes. And I agree, most of the characters are reasonable, emotionally deep and realistic characters meaning you can sympathise with them, understand their struggles and make yourself feel like you truly are fighting alongside them in a chaotic post-apocalyptic world. But notice how I said "most". Now I don't have a unique or witty way of saying this so I'm just going to do what every other over-dramatic person in this situation would do, that being to say it as it is but with caps lock on so that I can emphasise my point: ZOEY IS ONE OF THE WORST VIDEO GAME CHARACTERS EVER CONCEIVED BY MANKIND AND I WISH SHE WAS THE ONE THAT DIED INSTEAD OF- whoops almost just spoiled the end of a 15 year old  game everyone has definitely already played by now there, remind me not to do that again when I do another negative review. Anyway here's why.

I don't know if saying that Zoey is a badly written character is an unpopular opinion or whatever, but I do wanna say no offence to the writers or voice actor playing Zoey in the slightest, the writers did an incredible job in other places and the voice actor did a great job in general. Zoey just feels like a side character in an 80's text-based adventure game, so whether the writers were being overworked with 2 hours of sleep when making her or she was made by a 12 year old on a "bring your son/daughter to work day", I wouldn't be surprised either way. But what makes Zoey such a bad character? Well I promise I will actually answer that question this time in the next paragraph.

I want you to consider the other characters in Left 4 Dead 1 to start. You've got Louis, a successful business man with no combat experience in the slightest, and who probably has a pill fetish if the L4D community is a reliable source. There's Francis, a biker dude not used to working in a team with strangers, but is still willing to lend a hand to the group of survivors he has found himself in. And then there's Bill, a war veteran who clearly has a lot of experience with combat and gunplay, but zombies is a whole other story for him. Now try and describe Zoey's character. This is problem #1, Zoey is a boring character with nothing unique or distinct about her. She's just some random person who ended up in the zombie apocalypse alongside three other far more interesting characters. Now I get it, complaining that she has little backstory and saying that that alone is the reason why she is a bad character is a harsh thing to say, which is why I would also like to bring up the fact that she has basically no character development at all, both in changes to her as a person as well as traits she adopts throughout. Now admittedly, this is a part of Left 4 Dead 1's story that was lacking a bit, there is barely any character development in general, but in this case, you'd think they'd go all in on Zoey having the character development, but in the end even Francis ends up having more than her. Zoey is more one-dimensional than a Back 4 Blood character. In fact, look at Left 4 Dead 2: pretty much every character is unique and changes their attitudes to the zombies, each other and the impact of the apocalypse on their futures, something Zoey seems to be physically incapable of doing. Now I'm going to change the subject out of fear of repeating myself again.

Whether Zoey also looking like a really boring character as well as playing like one was intentional or not I don't know because I'm not a secret agent at valve trying to see whether people would care about Zoey dying in Left 4 Dead 3 coming out in around 20 years time. I know it sounds bizarre, but hear me out. Just by looking at the characters you can see how equipped or unequipped each character is for the zombie apocalypse, from the one in a business suit to another in full army uniform. Zoey is wearing a bland red jacket and jeans. Again, I get it, maybe her looking like a regular person was intentional to show just how unpredictable the outbreak was and how any one of us could be in such a situation any day now. Still though, what are we supposed to make of that? That she likes wearing that particular kind of outfit? The plain features don't say much in terms of her non-existent personality or her interests of literally nothing, unless it's meant to represent youth? In which case, ok, but why make that her entire character? Anyway, you're probably wondering why I mentioned earlier about her playing like a  boring character given how the character difference is completely cosmetic and each character plays the same. Well no offence to the voice actor once again, but the actual lines given for Zoey really don't help with character building or establishing her as a human being capable of doing human being things. Also I don't know if anybody else experiences this, but why does the Zoey AI absolutely hate me? No joke, when I play singleplayer, Zoey always shoots the witch whenever possible, shoots gas canisters when teammates are nearby, uses the only medkit on herself when she has the most health of the entire team (usually in the green too) and completely refuses to revive teammates, even when all the infected are dead. As if hating Zoey couldn't get any easier.

I think one of the reasons I hate Zoey so much is just seeing how well the characters in Left 4 Dead 2 were done. L4D2 probably has my favourite cast of multiple main characters of any video game due to just how contrasting they are in addition to how well they go together. watching as Roachelle basically becomes like a mother to the entire group despite clearly having no experience with that kind of thing before, or seeing how Nick goes from being a snide asshole to everyone to really letting his light shine through in their darkest moments is really heartwarming, even in a grim zombie-ridden world. Coach and Ellis' humour despite their worst fears coming to fruition is also charming, making these characters not only easy for each other to love, but for the player to love too. It's a shame that Zoey never got this treatment, sure there was not much potential when you really summarise her character, but considering how much less inspiration there might have been for other valve characters, I know they could have done so much better.

I know valve won't see this because they despise listening to their community, especially on the topic of their games, but at least they lay the foundations for wonderful communities to sprout in their wake. If only I could bring myself to give this beautiful game a positive review, unfortunately Zoey exists. So yeah, TL;DR: Zoey sucks.

When did it leave Early Access? Seriously, I want to know. The game is just as unpolished and ugly as it was in Early Access mode. Sure, I get it, EAHM doesn't have the same sized market as FM, but seriously; everything about this game is seven years behind. The interface is ugly and outdated, the game simulations are only 2d overhead (3d tv broadcast angle would be so great), players keep dumping the puck from their own zone resulting in a lot of icing calls and players struggle to accept passes at the point making a little figure skating pirouette; a play that most of the time ends up offside. Even when the man on the point is wide open and the pass is tape2tape. The game/sim speeds has very little variation: It's very slow, slow, somehow slower and speedoflight. It's difficult and time consuming navigating through all the in-game-menus (and at times its unresponsive as you have to left-click the choices half a dozen times before the page changes) and the need to confirm changes every time you look at your tactics, shortlist, free agency etc ,even if changes weren't made, is simply annoying. The lack of an established community where you can share succesful tactics you've created, custom designed jerseys  or AAR is a major let down. I mean, there is a community but it's SO empty. The boards are pretty much ghost towns. Even real players playing this game, the way proffesional soccer players play FM, would make the experience somewhat better. If you play FM you will know exactly what I mean. 

Entry-level contracts are also broken in the NHL but that might just be a bug in the rosters I downloaded.

My teams seem to always have trouble keeping pucks out of the net but I'll give EAHM the benefit of a doubt on this one and assume that A)my goalies are just that bad B)my tactics are just that bad C)A&B. I'm leaning towards A because I have experimented a lot and my skaters are stacked while my goalies are usually mediocre.

[i] So would I reccomend this game?[/i] [B] I have in the past touted just how excited I was to own this game "The game is addicting although it's very raw but only because it's in early access". [/B] Is what I would say, telling people to be patient. [U]But know I don't feel the same way. I actually [B]feel cheated[/B] and [b]betrayed[/b].[/u] Everything that I hoped and expected would be updated wasn't. If you're not hockey mad then stay away. If you enjoy this concept then play FM. sure it's made and published by the same companies but it's so much better.

I just finished the game and in my opinion it is criminally underrated. I don't know how it was released but now it runs really well (even on a Steam Deck) and looks awesome. The story is good, I mean... we're taking sci-fi/survival horror here, so pretty much complies with the standard. 

The game is linear with good pacing and I mean this as a good thing. The game is 10 hrs long, so no overstaying it's welcome - also good.

The one thing that I think has created controversy is the fighting... and yeah it can feel somewhat weird at times, specially with bosses, but it's decent. It can be somewhat frustrating when a horde is attacking you but hey, in what survival game this isn't the case?
To be honest, I think I appreciate the fact that this game is not a simple RE4 clone, I hope more developers try new things. Survival Horror games often had not so comfortable ways of playing, and that was not seen as a bad thing. I think that's because surviving in a difficult environment is not supposed to be easy. Tank controls in RE, Silent Hill's bad shooting and melee weapons and slow movement in Fatal Frame are some examples of this.

All in all, I think this is a good to very good game that deserves more attention from the fans of the genre. I enjoyed this game more than I did Dead Space Remake... well, maybe that's because I had already played the trilogy and it felt like the same thing, but anyway... if you like the genre I think there is a very good chance you'll enjoy this game, give it a shot.

review_text:
An interesting Metroidvania with survival aspects and rather difficult on the higher difficulties. Item usage is a big part of this game and you don't get increased movement options and abilities like in other metroidvanias, but there are a wide variety of spells and items with different play styles that still makes the game entertaining.

As mentioned in other reviews, the combat is pretty slow and there are no iframes meaning that you get one shot by pretty much every multi-hit attack in the game which can be annoying, but it is fun to plan out which items can best counter different enemy types which is where a lot of the strategy comes in.

One complaint that I do have is that because combat is slow and getting hit once is really punishing, there is no reason to use any melee weapon other than a dagger since it's the only weapon fast enough to reliably get in melee hits and this makes all other melee weapons practically useless which is unfortunate since there are some interesting weapons available that you can't really use. 

Magic is versatile and fun and there are multiple items that allow you to use magic more later on in the game. 

Overall, this is a pretty fun game and I recommend it.

Want to cause the deaths of over 15 people as a 7 year old boy? Want some easy achievements? This is the game for you. You'll get all but 2 achievements in 5-6 hours and the other two will take 40 afk hours. I actually found this game very fun and funny to play. The story is decent and the game is well made.

There is literally not even 10 hours of content let alone 40. They should replace the 20 hour with a 10 hour and replace the 40 hour with something fun like "Drink out of the fountain in the garden".

Chapter 15 also gives you at least one breakable object so you can farm those there. All achievements stack throughout failed runs so you can fail all you want to get the gun one for example. 

Play the game. It's $1 right now so it's 100% worth it. You'll probably enjoy it.

review_text:
Since there's no neutral option between a Negative and a Positive review i'll stick with a Positive one because even with some flaws here and there, overall this game was still a fun experience at the end of the day.
So here are some problems from the top of my head that makes me not have loved playing this as much as i wanted to:

First, here's the biggest problem of them all, the constant need to open the inventory menu every 10 seconds as you end up needing a different type of weapon in order to fight an specific enemy that's unfair or too hard with your previous set.

Second, with the help of the previous problem, the dull combat gets highlighted further as you start to notice the tiresome pattern of opening your inventory, searching for a specific weapon in a mess of an order, dodge the enemy attack, kill them and then in the next enemy repeat the process, including switching weapons.

Third, this is kinda underwhelming in my opinion, but the resources of this game are actually LIMITED, you'll get off a boss fight or a difficult corridor section and you'll reach a save point and feel safer until you realize that your HP and you MP don't recharge for free at all, never, the only way to recover basic resources is by either using weapons that heal you or buying potions, which takes us to the problem that you'll interact with a vendor and notice that you can only buy from him 20 bombs or something and then never anymore, it's gone, if you waste every dynamite in the game, then that's it.

There are some other minor things that you can choose to nitpick in this game, but honestly i'm fine with the rest, and even with these problems i've stated, i've had fun and seeing the endings and the entire journey made me happy to have played it to begin with, it's a cool game to play if you like it's type, there's some very nice music tracks here and there, mostly to the ending parts, and the biggest seller of the game is definitly it's BEAUTIFUL pixel art mixed with some modern lighting and other post-processing VFX, just don't expect TOO much of the game and you'll enjoy it, that's all.

review_text:
A game that is brutal for all of the wrong reasons.

There is no in game tutorial or help files. There is nothing on their website beyond forums. You have to pause the game and Google to find how anything works.

You get messages/warnings about stuff going on but you can't click on them and go to the location. A monster is attacking a building but to find out which one you have to scroll across the whole screen to find it. A person is starving but there is no way to know where or who it is.

You can't tell the monsters from your people. The pixel art is too low quality to tell the vast majority of monsters from your people and there is nothing in the UI to help. If you hover over a monster it get's a red circle but this isn't always there. Monsters get lost in the art of the buildings and you aren't able to pick them out. Add to this if you cast a spell or a fire elemental sets something on fire and it's just a screen full of nonsense where you can't tell your people from the monsters.

The sourcing of materials is horrific. A piece of wood can be on the ground next to something that needs 1 piece of wood but the colonist will go across the map to get wood from where else. I built a wood storage area near where I was going to build other stuff, the settlers still went to the other side of the map to get stuff and ignored the storage. 

Pausing the game covers the screen and doesn't let you look for stuff. You know the stuff like who is hungry, what building is getting destroyed, and where or where could those monsters be.

They mention RimWorld on the store page, buy that instead of this. It's brutal and fun. Plus it has support for mods so if there is something that annoys you chances are someone has already fixed it.

This game truly stands out with its remarkable gameplay dynamics. While it predominantly centers around the art of sniping, it introduces elements of stealth into the mix, enhancing the overall experience. The game unfolds through a series of contracts, each teeming with diverse objectives to undertake. Although the total count of missions may not be exceedingly high, the depth of engagement within each mission cluster ensures that you invest a substantial amount of time in exploration and execution. The size of the in-game map is commendable, offering ample terrain to traverse and conquer.

A notable highlight lies in the animation quality, particularly when a well-aimed shot pierces through an enemy's cranium—an aspect executed with satisfying precision. The game's environmental design adds a layer of immersion, such as the authentic sensation of one's character treading on frozen snow, further enhancing the sense of realism.

Completing each contract demands a significant time commitment, and the game intelligently provides the option to pause and resume later, tracking your progress with a percentage indicator. What distinguishes this game is its ability to immerse players so thoroughly in their missions that the surrounding world fades into the background. The freedom to explore within each area, methodically eliminating foes and accomplishing objectives, underscores the game's sense of autonomy. The map design, while not overly elaborate, remains effective, ensuring easy accessibility to your mission goals.

Moreover, securing this game during a sale yielded immense satisfaction, reinforcing the value of the purchase. Without reservation, I extend my enthusiastic recommendation for this title to any gaming enthusiast seeking an engaging and rewarding experience.

review_text:
The Callisto Protocol is a lot like Dead Space! Or is it... Follow Jacob Lee, a new inmate locked up in Black Iron Prison, where he bears witness to an outbreak of zombie-like creatures that wreak havoc on the prison. Get up close and personal with some brutal melee action to dismember and destroy the foes in your path as you try to find out just what the hell is going on.

Similar to Dead Space, you play Callisto Protocol in a third-person perspective walking around a dark and creepy environment. Similar to Dead Space, you'll occasionally be assaulted by three to five creatures of nefarious origin and tasked with dismembering them as swiftly as possible. Similar to Dead Space, you can also yeet and pull shit around with a tele-kinetic gravity arm tool thing. Similar to Dead Space, you can keep track of your health via a segmented bar on your back that you can refill with syringe item pickups, and similar to Dead Space you can find said pickups by stomping on an enemy's corpse. Similar to Dead Space, there's also a mysterious cult-like origin to the zombie beings that assail you. And yet with all these similarities to Dead Space, with all these moments where you go "I feel like I've played this game already", Callisto Protocol still manages to separate itself to a decent degree. The primary thing being that Callisto Protocol is incredibly melee-based, with a focus on counter-attacks and dodging and weaving through the swings of the enemy. The big benefit of this is that you really get to fully immerse yourself in the violence, gore, and horror of the action going on around you. And while I love Dead Space, this variation of a classic formula is still really fun to mess around with.

There are some downsides to The Callisto Protocol. For one, the combat can get a little repetitive after a while, as once you figure out the optimal block-dodge-strike sequences the game feels a tad "figured-out". To make up for this the game introduces a lot of new enemies and variants, most of whom feel exciting to encounter (we do not talk about Two-Head holy fuck what a boring enemy). The story definitely leaves a lot to be desired. Ironically, Dead Space actually has a really solid story at least for the first two games, whereas Callisto Protocol is about 9 hours of your protagonist going "what the hell is going on???????" followed by a final chapter of exposition dump and a god-awful ending. One of your primary antagonists has so much beef with you and for frankly no reason considering you've interacted for all of twenty minutes together. The DLC actually wraps up the main game's ending really well for the most part and offers a much better resolution in terms of gameplay and story, but considering this is locked behind a DLC paywall this feels really scummy. The gore is pretty solid, but the blood effects could be better for the type of the game it is and the advertised gazillions of ways your character can die don't really feel that amazing. If anything, you might see a grand total of like, 8 different animations in the whole story, as half the time an animation won't even play and your character will just flop over dead. Finally, the environmental layout feels really cheesy and slapped together. While it's graphically well-developed, it's also filled to the brim with cheap jumpscares and shimmy sequences (you will crawl through so many vents). Also what the hell kinda prison is this, why are there just random walls of spikes and sawblade machines of gore and destruction (besides to give the player some environmental tools to kill enemies with). 

And yet, with all that being said, I gotta say:

The Callisto Protocol's kinda fun.

Does it feel at times like a pretty inferior product to the game it so frequently emulates? Does it get redundant? Does it feel less horror-focused and more cheesy gore action movie at times? Yes to all these things. But if you can get it on a steep discount, say $20 or less, I'd say it's pretty worth it. Just set your expectations low, and go in just expecting to wail on some zombies for a few hours and experience some brain candy popcorn fun.

review_text:
A fun enough survival horror with strong (if not simplistic) brawler element that works well in a three-dimensional space, The Callisto Protocol is rightfully a divisive game, though one worth buying at a discount. This is a shame since the game play of the melee combat is actually good, or at the very least promising if there is to be a sequel. However, do not go expecting a Dead Space experience in terms of either combat or storytelling or comparable atmosphere.

Pros:
+Genuinely fun melee system incorporating weaves, combos, and firearms in a way that works far better than what was expected.

+Atmospheric setting that comes with being in a prison on an icy and dead moon.

+Environmental kills with the GRP are very satisfying.

+Enemy mutation adds a level of danger and depth to the combat.

Cons:
+Awful boss fights (Two-headed, Ferris) require a very different play style in terms of combat outside of the melee system that defines over 90% of the game, turning the game into a mediocre 3rd person shooter. 

Note to all prospective game developers: If the bosses of your games have a different playstyles than the rest of the enemies, then it is likely a bad boss battle. Don't make most of your bosses be platformers in a turn-based game.

+Nonsensical environmental storytelling that makes for an uninteresting world to explore. Like really, the prison went to shit in like what, a few hours tops? Compare this to Dead Space where it is implied (albeit inconsistently) that it took around a few days for the USG Ishimura to reach a similar level of destruction, or even weeks in the remake. It makes no sense why there are barricades, why there are widespread fires.

Uninteresting world. We learn very little about how the prison operates beyond it is just a front for experimentation, but we hardly hear from the prisoners themselves or even most of the workers about the day to day. By the time the game proper starts, most everyone is dead. For a gameplay mean to evoke the brawling and gritty aspects of prison life, this game merely takes place in a prison setting, but not a prison.

+Story leaves much to be desired in terms of its characters (Jacob's underdeveloped character arc regarding guilt, Dani's entire character, Elias' entire character)

+Making the ending of the game actual DLC.

+Lack of a good range of enemy design and game play that adds to the base gameplay.

review_text:
[b]Hakuouki: Kyoto Winds[/b] is a remaster of the game "Hakuouki", originally released on PS2 in 2008. I'm not a fan of dating simulators, but that game caught me because of  history of Japan in Edo Period. I was pleasantly surprised that there are no kisses, words of love or erotic content, only hints. This is a naive, in some places stupid story about friendship, self-sacrifice in the name of duty and love. I as a person with a heart of stone, can say for sure - nothing caused my tears no matter how awful the ending was. I guess, the game is mainly oriented towards romantic and dreamy female players, and it would be foolish to demand something brutal, terrible and cruel to a nervous tic. 
[i]There are 12 routes (three endings for each character). In total: [b]36 endings.[/b]

Recommendable  routes(IMHO): Hijikata, Harada, Toudou, Nagakura, Iba, Yamazaki, Sakamoto and Kazama's.

[u] Pros: [/u]
+ 12 romanceable guys,  so you'll definitely have your favorite at the end of the story.
+ Fully-voiced dialogues (except main hero) in Japanese language, not just a few phrases. This part is more important for me than anything else. 
+ Nagakura's  seiyū. Gosh, this guy did a wonderful job voicing him. Every time he put a goddamn smile on my grumpy face. 
+ "The Comedy Trio": Harada, Toudou and Nagakura. Without a doubt - best part of the game.
+ Fascinating  CG's. I bet artist sold his soul to the Devil for such talent. I wish I could draw like that one day.
+ Opening  theme "Ruri no Sora e". Already added in my playlist, but other musical composition  aren't especially memorable.
+ Lenght. My first walkthrough of Hijikata's route took about  10 hours. 
+ Mini- encyclopedia. If something causes questions, the game will explain.

[u]Cons: [/u]
- To play other route you must skip tons of text you read before. 
- Cannot skip credits after route was finished. I don't mind to read  it at first, but I decided  to beat up all achievements, so pretty annoying . It was fixed at "Edo Blossoms".
- Sanan's route. I have no clue why his route was added  in the game. He enjoys the fact that he is no longer a human and I fully agree with him: he is inhumanly boring. I'd like to romance Takeda instead.

review_text:
"Samorost 2" is a point-and-click game that tells a surreal story of a space gnome whose dog just got kidnapped by mischievous aliens. You will help the gnome to find its dog by solving different kind of puzzles. This game has an interesting plot, enhanced graphics with full-screen support, beautiful art, humouros sound effects, engaging puzzles and 13 achievements.
It's a short game as it took me only 20 minutes to finish it and get all the achievements (all the achievements can be acquired in one sitting). It has only one ending and there is a save feature, so you can restart or continue the game from a selected chapter. I would give it a 2/10 difficulty rating as the gameplay is minimal and the instructions are pretty clear during the whole game (you need to solve the puzzles and finish the story).
After playing "Samorost 1", which is a free-to-play game on Steam (you can find it here - https://store.steampowered.com/app/1580970/Samorost_1/), I decided to try more games from this developer. 
"Samorost 2", released in 2009, is the second game from the trilogy (you can find the third game on Steam as well) and it  has been developed by Amanita Design (Jakub Dvorsky's indie game studio), same company responsible for other well-known titles such as "Machinarium" or "CHUCHEL". In this game you will need to guide a space gnome on a quest across a couple of bizarre asteroids in order to rescue your dog from some aliens who kidnapped him. As you explore the asteroids and meet their strange inhabitants, you'll have to solve a few puzzles in order to progress. 
I didn't encounter any issues while playing the game and I was very much impressed by the beautiful visuals. The game's backgrounds often combine organic with inorganic elements and each scene in the game contains movement. The music (composed by Tomáš Dvořák) was extremely relaxing and created a wonderful atmosphere to just sit back and relax while solving the puzzles. The puzzles were not too difficult, although difficult enough that it presented a bit of a challenge. The story was really cute and well represented without the use of any word dialogue (there is only a little voice-acting in form of non-legible utterances).
As a recommendation for developer, I would like to suggest adding a hint button which may improve the experience for a lot of players. I would also like to mention that I got this game on a sale (for 99 eurocents) and I think that its initial price (of 4.99 euros) is a little too high for 20 minutes of gameplay.  
All things considered, I will definitely try more games from this developer and I would recommend this game to players that like surreal games or to the casual players that are trying new games/doing playthroughs.
If you want, you can check my full game playthrough here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JjnsCRI9WEM&ab_channel=Spartakus

After being frustrated with the heavily compressed audio in the remastered version I had for PS4, I decided to switch to the original version for this playthrough and, so, bought it here. As a result, I don't think I can recommend either version offered here on Steam, enthusiastically. If you do play through the game on PC, I say go with the remaster. The compromised audio quality is a huge issue, especially considering how spectacular the audio is in Bioshock. But, it's better than soldiering through the myriad issues I found on the original version.

review_text:
Three hours into the game and already several critical issues became apparent. First of all, your keybind resets every time you close the game. 

Second, the game encourages close quarters action despite being centered around stealth and sniping. The map may appear big but most of the time you're forced to be positioned at awkward angles whether vertically or horizontally, and with foliage and snowstorm obstructing you half the time. Granted, your polygonal eagle eye skill helps a little. 

What does not help however, thirdly, is that enemies disappear at a distance! You finally find the perfect sniping spot with a clear view of the enemy base only to find it completely devoid of activity! Back to sneaking and meleeing. 

Fourthly, mines travel like 2 cm when thrown, which means you basically must be directly on the spot in order to set mine, which means that if you enjoy trapping you'll often end up screwing yourself because you cannot disarm it when backtracking or even mark its location. Enemies also rarely send units to investigate when you're detected and instead just hide behind cover for all eternity. Meaning less chance your traps get triggered. 

Finally, Bounties tend to be right in your exfil location so quite often you'd end up activating the mission just as you wish to end your gaming session by approaching the exfil. You're forced to do the bounty then and there, otherwise countdown ends with you failing. You'll then have re-enter the map again later just for the bounties.

Pros: The high tech gadgets are fun and being a CryEngine game gunshots feel very satisfying. 

Cons: Previous installments felt more enjoyable, but if I wanted to play a sniper game it's still Sniper Elite. If I wanted to play an action game on CryEngine I'd just go back to Crysis, which still had better sniping. It's an action shooter where every mission is a sniping mission.

review_text:
I never used to be a "story driven game" kind of person, but after playing a few conventional games that had much more prominent stories and getting really engrossed in them, I decided I would try out this game since it was hailed as one of the best indie story games. Maybe I'm just not actually that into story games, but this game just wasn't fun. I didn't have an emotional reaction to the game like so many people did, which could be because I'm unfeeling or something but was probably just due to the shortcomings of the game. 

The gameplay was essentially nonexistent, essentially just point and click to progress the dialog. It didn't really need to be a game, and I don't think I would have lost anything from the experience if I had just watched a video of someone playing the game. In fact, one thing that would have been improved in that scenario would be the absolutely terrible controls. For a game that is almost entirely mouse based, I never thought it would be possible to fight against the controls so often and to such little avail. I never got used to them, even after 3 hours. The writing was generally just distracting, with unfunny (and at this point dated) humor sprinkled randomly and unsuccessfully at inopportune times throughout the game. The story didn't have any real payoff other than (mild spoilers) [spoiler] she's neurodivergent and he had trauma [/spoiler] which are not very interesting story elements, especially because the characters explicitly don't talk about them. By the time the game was wrapping up, I was really just hoping it would end so I could go to bed. 

Ultimately, I guess what I have learned is that this genre is not for me, because this was supposed to be the best the genre had to offer and it just wasn't very good. I guess I'll go back to looking for games that have fully developed stories [i] and [/i] well thought out gameplay mechanics, but they're a lot harder to come across than stuff like this.

review_text: hooooooh as much as i'd LOVE LOVE LOVE to recommend this game i just dont feel like its worth playing in its current state. While this is an early access game and i shouldnt be ragging on it too hard, this game has a lot of fatal flaws to it that need to be addressed before release. A good example of this is wall running, Wall Running is a very fun feature to use, and crucial to multiple stages of the game, even the first one you need to beat to play the game at all. But wallrunning only works about half the time i try it and is very finicky to use, it only works about half the time and its inconsistent if you will grip to a wall, you also are seemingly unable to grip to walls if your double jump is exhausted. The stage designs while good, arent very many, with a simple loop of 4 quick stages every run, and no way to end a run besides dying. while most of the summit shrine rewards are good some of them like Drudgie Birthday Party are unexplained by both the game and the wiki and seemingly do nothing useful. Melee weapons are far too infrequent and break too easy for a weapon that you'll only find potentially once every 4 stages. One final complaint i have is that Sprint Chests aren't explained at all, they dont have a timer to tell you how fast you need to go, even when ive been going as fast as i can i never get them. For positives this game is VERY fun to play, and would be easily a top 10 if my complaints were addressed. moving around so quickly and being able to swoop in and melee enemies feels AMAZING and the tech with build a bang'd guns is also super fun to use, along with the guns themselves being fun. I love the variety of guns, recently i played arena and saw a gun i'd never seen before in 5 hours of play and it was super fun to blow up whole groups with it, and i hope i continue to find cool new stuff ive never found before while playing! all in all, this game would be an easy 10/10 if it just had issues fixed and more stages added.

review_text:
The moral of this game is microtransactions.

You can do everything to level 65 however the game ends at 50 for free characters. After 50, you need to pay around $15 for the next level ship and various other things if you failed to 'spec' your character correctly. In addition, there are about 20-30 ship variations which means to unlock them all on a single character would be very expensive.

End game content is plenty but the role system is broken. Everything revolves around DPS with tanking and support defunct. Especially when some factions seem to just bypass shields entirely.

All in all, it's a broken non-social MMORPG. It'd be better as a solo player game.

review_text:
Unfortunately, I am having too much trouble with the interface which is everything in a management simulator.  If I try to alt-tab out while in fullscreen mode I cannot resume the game and instead get a black screen and am forced to exit out of the game.  In windowed mode on my widescreen monitor, the bottom is cutoff and I cannot do such things as respond to trades.  Clearly, not everyone is having this problem but I have looked it up and I am not the only one who encounters this with no remedy.

Beyond my computer specific issues, the interface is gets in the way of itself.  Secondary windows remove certain menu options without being clear that you are in a second window.  The inability to sumulate multiple days at a time without relinquishing duties, the general slowness of simming, the general obtuseness of ratings, this is not an easy game to get into.  That is not to say there is not value here, clearly many have found rewards in EHM, but there are steep obstacles to enjoyment and I personally could not get past them.

review_text:
Bonelab is to Boneworks what Garry's Mod is to Half-Life 2. Kind of.

It's a fun little side adventure in the VR-inside-of-VR world of MythOS with some interesting set pieces that are more adventurously designed compared to the levels of Boneworks. The remarkably short story feels more like an add-on to the sandbox, but forces itself to be front and centre for far too long before letting you play with all of the fun stuff. Kind of like being made to watch an hour long instructional video on how Steam works before you're allowed to open your library. It's not an offensively bad story by any means, but it went through one ear and out of the other the whole time I was playing.

Unfortunately, when compared to Garry's Mod's own mod support, Bonelab is far, very far, behind. Mods are handled through Mod.io - for the sake of compatibility with standalone headsets, and to simplify mod development as much as possible.

The ripcord, the iconic little character-model-changer device on your character's arm, is something that you can unfortunately only edit much later on - meaning you have to finish the entire campaign, which is a colossal PITA to play through if you only want to play with the sandbox and mods.

It's somehow the best VR sandbox while aggravatingly trying to not be just a VR sandbox.

Soooo .... This game is frustrating. If you are not a sadomasochist then just don't even try this game. No kidding. I am 36 hours in this game as of writing. I installed a patch on PC so I could do saves when I want. It still is not good enough to rescue this game.

One the graphics are beautiful. The story lines are long, very long, too long to a point they are boring. But I kept up with it. I played PAST the wedding and ended up in the castle. I won't spoil. but wow... I was a pretty happy player making weapons at the blacksmith and doing side quests and upgrading my equipment. 

The combat is not just clunky, it is extremely clunky. If you played any FPS games then ... wait no that doesn't help you at all. I tried with mouse and controller (95%) but the combat just doesn't work. I don't get it. I practiced with tomcat, many times. Enemies just charge you, then you run out of energy and you cannot do anything except walk back until they hit you again. If you hit them, even with 'combos' you hardly do damage. If you survive a simple combat you are wounded and need to heal. You need to pay dearly for healing potions or make them yourself which is not just boring, it is also frustrating. I play a game for fun, not to learn how to add which herbs in which order in a pot ; let me play blacksmith and with the money I earn I will buy the potions. Forget about that - you won't make enough - even if you learn the Bearded Axe recipe and make decent money. I normally slept off the damage, wasting time and what not.

Back to the game play. Some quests have perfect instructions what to do, even though you have to find it in the world - that's fine. I understand not every quest can be easy, but BOY WHAT IS THE GAME FRUSTRATING once you get to the big castle after the wedding.

During the early game play I smashed my controlled on the table, breaking it. I never had so much rage in my entire 20+ year of gaming life. What a FRUSTRATING game. I really want to try to be a better man, but sorry, after I found a quest was 'locked' or 'broken' (by design') I gave up. I think I will give up. Maybe I'll try more after reading AGAIN AND AGAIN guides online how to do things. It's not that I want to finish the game in 10 minutes, I'm 36 hours in and I'm sure other people could get to the point where I am in half the time or less. I did a ton of side quests, got my dog back, have a high level of crafting, made easily 50 or more Axes and horseshoes - I'm not speed running this game.

But again - this game is basically unplayable without guides. And guess what - there are MANY guides online. Guess why? Because figuring some things out would be IMPOSSIBLE without sinking hundreds of hours in the game for even the first initial part.

I am not stupid, I am pretty handy with my controller in most games. From Racing to FPS to say Diablo 2/4 etc. I do not consider myself an eSport expert, but I'm no noob neither. The combat is infuriating. The tutorial is extremely limited and offers little help. You're thrown in the deep , have to figure it out and then you die and can START OVER AGAIN often losing many HOURS of 'work'. This game feels like work. That's a good description.

It is GREAT to walk the landscape and enjoy the view, but most quests are just there to keep you busy and then lead you to FRUSTRATING ENCOUNTERS with enemies or wildlife like wolves which you can cut 4 times with a good sword and they still run around as healthy. 

Don't spend money on this game. I think I paid around $40 for it and while that sounds low, it is about $35 too much for wasting my time and causing me high blood pressure.

I know most people are very positive about this game - this review is to warn new people to not try this and become frustrated as well and leave without even dropping a negative review - I can only think that is why this game has so much positive feedback.

Just watch some nice Youtube walkthroughs or so, save yourself the money and frustration. Don't say I didn't warn you.

Note ; the game barely has started after 20 hours of gameplay. I don't know how someone can give a positive review after just 20 hours, in THIS game. It feels most reviews are fake.

review_text:
A tribute to H.R. Giger, unfortunately way too short and only mediocre gameplay.

Visually clearly an hommage to the great H.R. Giger (creator of THE Alien), quite disturbing, rather alien, heavily sexualized and artistically well done. 
Gameplay itself on the other hand is rather disappointing, an attempt to combine puzzle games and 1st person shooter, but unfortunately failing in both aspects. The makers chose to try a very ambitious attempt by telling the whole story without any dialogue, but the storyline is as vague upon finishing as it was after 10 mins into the game. 
Even with having to repeat some parts more than once (yes, there is no saving option and check point placement is bad..) the game is played through in about 3 hours in total. Not worth purchasing at full price and even only having paid 20 Euros (incl. Artbook) I wouldn´t recommend buying this game unless you are a dedicated Giger Fan.

Why is it that looking away from two assassins make it so they go away?  What?
"OH NO, MY ONLY WEAKNESS, VICTIM LOOKING AWAY FROM ME FOR 10 SECONDS!"
That's dumb.  I hate it.
Also, a keypad unlocks the door when the code changes?  And THE CODE CHANGES!?
That's dumb.  I hate it.  That's not how security works.

review_text:
[h1]Doesn't feel finished. [/h1]
I like this game, I like a lot of the features that it has. The generational concept of the game play is fairly unique and well implemented. 
The world is cute. The ideas are all nice. The design is lovely. The problem is that it doesn't feel fleshed out.

 The NPC's all feel very much the same. They have "traits" but they don't seem to change much except the repetitive dialogue options that they have are a bit different than NPC's with other "traits". The family just sits on the stairs in my house instead of using the furniture or doing anything interesting. When someone dies you get an invitation to their funeral, but there is no indication of how they died and everyone at the funeral just has their regular interactions. It takes away from the community feeling and immersion.

You can only adopt one pet, but the game doesn't tell you that it just won't let you purchase anymore after you buy the first pet.  There are items that are meant to lead to a quest or something but have no purpose as of now because they devs haven't finished them. The mines are pretty boring as they are. 

The crafting takes an incredibly long time (all day long for one brick to cook?) 

If they can flesh this game out and adjust some of the time mechanics, it will be top tier. For now, I played for a couple of seasons of in game time and now things feel samey and I'm growing bored. I hope they can add some more as I think it has a lot of potential. 

I can recommend this game for about 15 hours of playtime, less if you grow bored easily, and more if the things that I listed above don't bother you.

In its current state, just don't bother honestly. Maybe if they release a hard mode to make the game's multiplayer remotely challenging or some way to play more than just 2 levels and a single boss for many, MANY, hours.

Even if you're still convinced you'd like it PLEASE wait for a sale. You'll feel better in the long run. $60 is downright absurd for what you get. Even worse, some elements for certain character's weapons in the base game are locked behind character DLC so you might spend even more if you really want some of your favorite characters as flexible as possible.

Just go play fatal bullet or something.
