review_text:
Rating: 8/10
Hakuoki Kyoto Winds is a good historical visual novel filled with a variety of interesting characters. Despite the lack of romance that one might expect from an otome game, the relationships are still compelling and you end up really caring about the characters. The gradual process of getting close with other characters feels natural. The plot is pretty good, following the Shinsengumi’s history over the course of 4-5 years and Chizuru’s (the MC's) experience living with them. 

There are some exciting action scenes, fun villains, and a bit of mystery regarding the MC’s background. Choices do matter in this game, as they determine whose route you end up on and whether you get a good, normal, or bad ending. A little butterfly icon pops up to let you know you’ve made a choice leading to a happy ending, which is handy. The different character routes don’t really diverge too much from the core story. The first 2-3 chapters are pretty similar regardless of route, though there are different side scenes that happen. A lot of Chapter 4 and 100% of Chapter 5 and the Epilogue will be unique to the route. The repetition can be a bit much, especially with 12 routes, though there is a skip button. You do tend to learn different information in each route, so aside from hanging out with a different character you also get a deeper understanding of the story.

Though Hijikata is the recommended first route, I would highly recommend not doing his route first if you would like to not hate the MC. The core story was good, but it was painful playing as the MC (the girl needs to get some self-respect and stop apologizing for her very existence, good grief). It took me a playing a few more routes before I actually started to like her. Her character can vary a bit by route, but I appreciate how when she decides to trust someone she is very steadfast and doesn’t waver. She will stand up for others (and sometimes herself *sigh*), and she cares deeply about the (future) love interest. She doesn’t have a vague crush, she is genuinely invested in their wellbeing. It was nice to see how in these turbulent times, her steadiness was something that was able to ground others. She provided genuine comfort to characters.

I did really enjoy getting to know these characters. The villains are fun too, I cheer whenever they show up. I really liked how each route fleshed out the story, helping us learn more about the characters and the mysteries happening. Each of the villains also gets highlighted in different routes, so you learn more about them as well. The main thing bringing the rating down is the repetitiveness and the slightly exasperating MC in some routes. Otherwise, Hakuoki Winds is pretty good.

review_text: After completing SH2:Remake from Bloober I was anxiously awaiting Cronos after its announcement trailer. I like many others love Dead Space and have always longed for something to fill that void, so Cronos looked promising. That being said, Cronos The New Dawn is an atmospheric, creepy, intense, and excellent survival horror experience. Survival Horror in the true sense- low resources, encounters that feel like life or death, and heart pumping bosses that really have you barely getting by with ammo. The difficulty is perfectly balanced, the more you play the more you understand how to handle situations best and although challenging at the start, by the end you are cruising by enemies. The story is interesting enough, the general mystery behind the disease and its relevancy to your character are what kept me engaged and the multiple endings and new game+ make replayability worth it. Definitely pick this up if you love horror, for it definitely is a standout amongst the current options out there right now! 2/2 for Bloober and I am happy they can be trusted within the horror space! Finally, performance was fine on my end, played through high settings 60 FPS and had no crashes or terrible hiccups, the occasional stutter when loading certain areas, but quickly smoothed over so nothing frustratingly bad.

I learned to play the game the way it mean to be played.
Learned that i needed to cover, stop, breath, reload, double check my map, then rush to kill a enemy.
Learned to conserve ammo, to swap weapons on right time, engage on long and close range...

[h2] Then, after some time, it was just a breeze leveling up there. [/h2]

Got my ascended level to like 40~50.
Time to go on Velmorne..

The same loop repeated. 
Specially on the "dead" part.
Omg... It repeated a lot on this map.
SO many times i died to the elements present there that... Wow...

After that, the difficulty, in my opinion, was fine.
The Castle gates was OK. To be honest, for me, wayyy easier than Velmorne.

The Witch Mountain was a total blast when i reached there.
It was a complete different mechanic, remembering a lot of Destiny 1~2 path to incursions, with a TOP TIER fight at the end.

[h2] Really loved it!!! [/h2] 

The optional content (Wailing Tower) was brilliant.
It's awesome the way it is, hope its expanded in the future.
REALLY hard. Was about ascension level 85 my first victory there. 

[h2] Finally, Witchfire is, with no doubt, on my favorite list. [/h2] 

Hope to come back soon!

review_text:
Why the mixed Reviews for Callisto Protocol?? 
HEHE WELL GLAD YOU ASKED, HERE IS WHY:
 
- TECHNICALLY ITS BEAUTIFUL , detailed textures, particle effects, lighting... BUT the game doesn't stand out in terms of art style, everything feels... Not very inspired, not unique and this technical strength isn't used to portray beautiful vistas or sceneries. 

- COMBAT is... Frustrating, to the point where I lowered the difficulty to a minimum just to go faster. Enemies have a ton of health, you don't have a ton of weapons/options, so it gets very repetitive. Enemies benefit from frames of invincibility when they vault over an obstacle or when they start to get up. They basically wait in line before fighting you, because the game knows you barely have any means to deal with groups, so it can be very tedious to deal with each individual in turn. BUT the animations are very well made and detailed. 

- THE STORY is serviceable, but very reminiscent of past Resident Evil games so do NOT expect subtlety. 

- GAME TIME is decent (8-10 hrs) but gets very repetitive because enemy variety is lacking, and the last segment is nonstop battle. 

- THE FEAR is pretty much non existent, but if that's your thing the game can be very gore.

All in all, it appears the game was already old when it came out, because it uses so many dated mechanics but other than that it holds on its own.. so giving a thumbs down would seem unfair, although if you really are on time constraints, you'd be better off playing the latest Resident Evil or Dead space games.

review_text:
Absolutely a must buy. Even so I give this 7/10. After you complete the intro you will unlock the "mission lobby" where you can meet other players, take missions, mod your weapons, mod your loadout, etc.

CONs:

    - no story 
    - no bHaptics feedback support (guys, get your act together, it takes like an hour to do this, at least for when you get 'picked up' by the big snowbies or when you get hit or are in an explosion please, for bonus points, add rumble for elevators, lifts, vehicles, etc.)
    -  you can't choose your avatar (wth not?)
    -  tutorial is insufficient (like not explaining that you can store your weapon and change loadouts prior to starting a mission, or how the loot boxes work, or why collecting the floppy disks is important, or how there is an in-game menu)
    -  no single player mode, forced team-combat, so this is basically a team-combat game
    -  AI voices even if a real player is playing that character (major nono)
    -  Very little content (only like 4 missions currently, however, I believe more will be added with the first season for free)

PROs:

    -  variety of enemies and boss fights
    -  sense of accomplishment and progression 
    -  looks and feels great (lots of improvements from Arizona Sunshine)
    -  roguish (normally I despise rogue-likes, but having things be a bit different on each run through is a really nice touch in this game)

Couple of bugs:

    o  There is a chance that your entire fireteam will not be loaded back into the same lobby when you return to "the hub", so you won't be able to hear each other over VOIP.  Fix this by having players in a fireteam be summoned to the same lobby instance as the teamleader. Also, have players be summoned to same lobby after accepting a team invite as well.

    o  You are able to enter a mission with ZERO weapons if you accidentally place all your weapons on the rack prior to start. 

    o One time I entered a mission with only one of my firearms, even though I was equipped with two prior to starting a mission (Only happened once though)

    o  It is possible for another player to accidentally be added to your fireteam when you start if you don't have at least two other people in your crew. Not really sure how this happened, not really a big deal, better than having an AI player.

Overall, despite some major flaws and badly needed additions or changes, this game was very stable, looks good, plays smoothly 95% of the time, and was lots of fun. Plan on putting in many more hours. In fact, probably going to go back to wired from wireless since I hate having to take a break to re-juice my charger.

review_text:
I do not recommend this game~ 🌹

Most people who pick this game up will want to play Multiplayer.
But here's the thing... You have to play the single player campaign to unlock characters.
The single player Missions take place on very large maps, which are obviously set up in a way for multiplayer.
So you spend so much time in single player running/dashing just to get to the next objectives.

Even crazier still, once you slog through all of the campaign missions and finally decide to go into Multiplayer, there are currently only 6 multiplayer maps (Will they add more later? Probably.) 
But here's the next kicker!!!!

Those maps are arranged by Player Level. That means if you want to gain the most exp for your Account, you'll always want to do the latest mission. Once you reach "end game," they decided to pair up two missions together in a single queue. So if you select it, it's random which of the two maps you get.
At first you'd think that's good for variety, but this also means you have to stare at the loading screens to figure out which map you are playing on in order to select the right element weapon for that mission. Even worse, some characters don't have access to certain elements. Klein for example, doesn't have access to the Electric element, so if you pick him and the map switches to the forest, there's nothing you can do about it and you are forced to play that mission suboptimally. 

Not only that, but as you progress through the player ranks, it gets harder and harder to gain experience for your Account. Which means you end up running the same 2 quests or bosses (which there are currently only 3, maybe 4 because they switch out the last remaining boss from only a queue of 3 bosses). 

Which again, You need to be a very high player rank just to select the highest boss to fight.
Think about that. You are stuck farming the same boss over and over again. 

The game is also EXTREMELY grindy, which wouldn't be a problem if the game was fun.
But some characters are just broken. For example, with Asuna it's almost always best to just spam Triangle while held down. Some characters play best just spamming Square. Completely nullifying their entire kit. 
The combat is also extremely clunky imo.

Even with it's own faults you might get some fun out of it for awhile.
But I personally believe that Alicization was the last best SAO game out of the entire series.
Even better than Fatal Bullet.

This game just needs to be fleshed out with more content to be worth $60.

review_text:
Yakuza 5 is called Yakuza 5 because you get to play 5 characters. Seriously though what the actual hell, as if the Devs thought Y4 did not have enough things to do for each playable character, they MADE SURE you had an obscene amount of things to do with each individual character. They looked at the previous game and just said "lets beef this thing up to the max and try to make the ultimate Yakuza game thus far".  

Dont play this game if you haven't played the Previous entries blah blah blah.

Yakuza 5 is an incredibly big improvement from Yakuza 4 in gameplay, minigames, side stories, substories (they are different!) and just about almost anything else in between. As a person who started playing the series from 0, I would say this game is the closest thing feeling wise to that one (0 is still by far the better game and still my favorite). So you might of noticed that I mentioned a few things that this game improved on, but I left out the main story from that category. The reason for that is because I Feel like the story in this game, although not terrible and honestly pretty ok, wasn't as hard-hitting or as cohesive as I would of liked it to be and felt like it was all over the place. To be honest, it was a little bit of a let-down compared to all the other games that I played in the franchise, and I feel like this happened because the devs were probably so focused on adding so many damn things to do in the game that they probably didn't have enough time or energy to develop the story just a little more to make it manageable and easy to follow. The main story overall just felt like a second thought and was predictable on certain occasions instead of it being a priority. It didn't help that each playable character took place in a completely different city so the story overall felt very split as they would explain the character first and what they are going through before getting back into the main story of the game. The main villain was also not that great, we've had much better.

The game has you starting off with Kiryu in Fukuoka which I think was a good choice from the previous game where you played him last. At the beginning of the game however, they make you do all these different things while teaching and showing you all the different stuff you can do to the point where if you dive deep into the side stories and sub-stories, you might forget completely that something is going on in the main quest. Kiryus gameplay was fun as he is such a solid fighter with the addition of new moves you can pull such as grabbing enemies when you finish a combo and overall the most balanced character. His side stories were pretty fun too as it has you driving a taxi and I really enjoyed the ones that had you racing against other opponents. The normal taxi missions though could have gone with having less of them as most of them were just you doing multiple choice questions from dialogue, so it got repetitive. If anything they should of cut the number of Taxi missions by half.

Right after you're done with Kiryu you go to Saejima which starts exactly the same as it did with the last game, and then the same cycle repeats with him as it did with Kiryu. Saejima combat wise is improved, he is still a heavy hitter that does a ton of damage with a wider range of move sets to your disposal, especially if you level him up and learn new abilities from your master trainer. His side story was one of the most enjoyable to me as you get to go out and hunt animals by being strategic as you need to be quiet when approaching a deer or with Bears being able to dodge your bullet which adds tension and forces you to land the perfect shot. My only complaint is that walking was pretty slow and the animation to set up traps and take them off got annoying as it dragged. Saejima was also the only character where you had 2 different places to travel to as the hunting side stories took place in a small village while everything else took place in the main City of Sapporo.

After you're done with Saejima you get to play... Get this... HARUKA! Which was completely different from all the other characters gameplay-wise. Haruka Does not fight but instead engages in dance battles which has you playing a rhythm game similar to karaoke. All of her side stories events are about the same thing with the exception of some where it does the same multiple choice questions you had to do with Kiryu and another one where you shake hands and answer questions while timing how long to hold the hand. As much as I appreciated Harukas part of the game, I think it dragged on for far too long because all the side stories were the same thing repeated 5 times over to the point where trying to complete it just felt like a menial task more than a fun quirky gimmick. I'm not sure why they gave Haruka the most side stories, but the game would of benefited if they just slashed that number by half just like Kiryus.

Akiyama Starts in the middle of Harukas chapter and I was actually relieved that he was the only character that didn't get side stories, you still have sub stories though and those were fine. Akiyama to me was probably the most fun character to play. He's quick, snappy with his kicks and they gave him a new ability where you can throw people in the air and whale on them. Akiyama felt like the closest thing to Dante from DMC being in this game. Him and Haruka also take place in Dotonbori so no new city for him which was honestly a relief as well.

Finally, the last character you play is a washed out Baseball Pro named Shinada. Out of all of the character's story and even the main Story of the game, I enjoyed his the most. I felt like he was relatable and felt bad for him a lot of the times because of his past and what he had to go through, there was also other times where I just felt like he was a complete idiot that doesn't have any common sense. His combat style was my least favorite, I did not like playing him and I did not like going through his section of the game because I just really did not enjoy how he fought. They advertise the character as a Weapon user but he's actually more of a Grappler and his way of fighting is just very odd. His Side stories were pretty enjoyable though as all it has you do is play in the batting cages, so if you like baseball you will like his Side stories. With his Part of the game they also introduced the best Character in all of the Franchise, Koichi Takasugi. I love that guy, he made me laugh a couple of times.

After you're done with everyone's story, the game throws you back in Kamurocho (Finally!) for the final chapter, and man do I love Kamurocho, I wish the game would just let you play there from the start instead of having you go on this wild goose chase collecting members. So besides the combat for each individual Character, I feel like This game also suffered from the same thing that Yakuza 3 suffered where enemies would just constantly block all the time, Blockuza was very apparent and alive in this entry. Normal Enemies wouldn't block as often but it still happened enough for me to notice and Boss fights... They all just blocked almost always. I don't understand what happened, Not sure if its a remaster issue or what but it was incredibly annoying fighting bosses at times, all I could do most of the time was just grab and throw them. Speaking of bosses, a lot of them were very poorly designed as some that I would fight would Spam the same move constantly without having any sort of variety. The game itself is fine. It's a short experience, really cute, and the puzzles mostly make sense (except for the last one). The problem is that it's not really a sequel to the original free Flash game Samorost, but a longer version of it. The first 60% is available online, for free, which means you're being charged $5-6 depending on your region for what amounts to half an hour of gameplay with a frustrating conclusion. And on top of that, it's made in Flash, which means you don't have to figure out where you can click, you can just hit tab and see the hotspots light up for you. For a commercial release, that feature [i]really[/i] should have been removed, as it destroys the immersion.

Play the free version online, and if you want the next chapter get this 90% off or as part of a bundle. It's not worth full price.

review_text:
It's a massive improvement from SGW3 and honestly i want to give positive review, but still left numerous annoyance from previous game. This game is try to be both HITMAN and it's 3rd person arch nemesis, Sniper Elite but ended up failed try to be both.

The graphics is absolutely beautiful and everything feels more finished than previous game.

The reticle system is the best of other sniper game, it have bullet drop & distance guide but you still need to aim exactly where to shoot, the game never tell you where the bullet gonna land. Its a perfect balance no too easy and not too hard, i wish Sniper Elite implemented this in some way

Unlike Sniper Elite, this game is more on realism side than fun with a HUGE ASTERISK, it's annoying and inconsistent as hell.

First of all AI, while it's improved from previous game, it still annoyingly inconsistent. Sometimes the enemies have no idea what happened around him, but sometimes a single shot to a lonely enemies, and suddenly other enemy from far away noticed it. I like the idea that enemies will bring binocular and can spot you from a far, but it's weird when everyone can do it (not just officer, heck idk what officer exactly do)

2nd this game seems run great & very optimized, until you ran out of vram and first thing they do is reduce draw distance on enemies which is stupid on sniper game, the enemies you try to snipe just gone just because you step back a few meters (this is also the reason why maximum shot distance you did in game never exceed 400m)

While i love the reticle system, the distance measurement system is not, i prefer the distance measured by the scope, not the tags. Also tagging HUD is not contrast enough with environment, it's hard to to check where is the enemiy tags

The gadget and skills is either should be give to player in the first place or just useless. Also i wish the drone didn't exist for both sides, player drones is useless 75% of the time, and enemy drone is just annoying.

The player manuverablility it's realistic except when sometimes you can't scale tiny obstacle and those tiny incline, stone, marble can totally block you up and you need to jump or stand up which is again annoying

The level design is good, with many variation, but it could be better or make it little bit more fun/engaging, and fast travel should not exist in game, instead player could choose infil point at beginning of the contract

In the end i want this game to succeed, but it need to fix a lot of issue, especially the draw distance optimization, manuverability over tiny obstacle & overall game design and balance

review_text:
Interesting Game with potential but can´t recommend due to wired gameplay design choice and bugs and clearly Beta.


Gameplay:
You pick a piece of land from a world map. Then you place your keep and drop some villagers and start collection ressources to build your town.
Most of the nights you are attacked by monsters and therefore have to build defenses.
The monsters spawn in a randomly placed piece of land labeld as corruption.
The wave of enemys get stronger and stronger and after 15 nights (the first year) you will loose due to massive power increase the monsters have.


Problems / bugs:
The game is not late game optimized. The longer the game runs and the bigger your town gets all the functions are breaking appart. Sometimes it takes a full morning just to build one building but you have 20 workers and full ressouces.

Building cheap bow towers is only for good for the first nights, because the more towers you have your AI will not be able to supply them with arrows. This is clearly a bug. I had 10 bow towers and two fully developed bowyers, they refuse to do anything.

Corruption spawns always the same amount of monsters regardless how big their town / area is. I attacked them early and nearly surrounded their spawn. I drove the corruption on the ground back. They only had one graveyard and 5 towers but they spawn the same amount like owning 20 graveyards.

You can not win on any map. You can not win against corruption. Neither by destroying their spawn nore by digging in and defending. Why? Because rebuilding the destroyed buildings takes too long. You just don´t have enough time to rebuild until the next night arrives. Maybe you manage to rebuild but next wave it stronger. You can´t win the arms race. Also if you dig in you will run out of stone and then you can not rebuild. So you must expend.
And destroying the spawn is impossible because building your town and reaching the spawn and building towers to defend just takes the first full year.

Once winter hits, it is game over.

Waymakers take way too long to build a path. Towers build a lot faster compared to a a stupid tile of path.

Ressource transport takes way too long if you base is far away from the building place.
(This is rediclious: You must expend to contain the corruption, but you can´t expend because your logistics fail, even with 25 workers running day and night).

In late game (day 15+) your golems just die so quickly to the enemy. The only golums that are useful are crystal golems because of their range attack. The wood and stone golems get eaten up.

No focus fire. In late game the enemy sends "fire golems" they will attack from range and burn your towers from save distance. You can not take them out by focus fire, because there is no focus fire. And your towers will always attack nearst target not "Target with highest priority". Even if your defense is able to hold of the wave these fire golems will kill some of your towers and you can´t rebuild in time.

You can´t attack corruption. During daytime i outnumber the enemy. I have 40 golems and turrets, during nighttime enemy sends 100 monsters. GG. Why can you not send your army of soldiers and golems to attack the corrution? Why do you even allow the monsters to build turrets? Monsters dont have to defend their base because you can´t even attack. LOL.

Game time with 1x is way toooo slow. I always run the game at 2x. Otherwise it takes ~12 hours to get to Day 15.



Improvements:
Fix the bugs above.
Fix the gameplay above.

Add logistics squad who just send ressouces from main base to small bases and do nothing else. So that you can create a stock pile clsoer to the frontline for faster building.
Add research so you can further improve your units, buildings and so on.


Hey dev! What is even the purpose of your game? Play until day 15 then transfer villagers to limbo. Then start new land tile and repeat? Your game makes no sense. ..

review_text:
Note: The world this occurred on was Traditional difficulty. I lasted a year and a season.

I understand difficulty is mean to be a big draw of this game, I understand the whole "spend ages then die" is supposed to be intended. But there is no world where suddenly losing a twenty hour village isn't painful, and not in a good way. I've spent the last thirty in game days gradually pushing back the corruption and gauging the response from the monsters every night, keeping in mind the warning from the tutorial hint that the corruption will fight back if I deprive it of room. Everything was fine until the last few days. I was managing the monsters alright every night, they got much tougher but it was nothing my defenses couldn't deal with. Until suddenly, the corruption stops getting pushed back by fire pits. Where it would basically melt before, now it just sticks around. So what would have been the final day of corruption got dragged out into one more night, except now the monster spawns were INSANE. I killed something in the ballpark of 300-900 monsters that kept pooling out of the small collection of MAYBE one hundred tiles, and now the monsters had several thousand health instead of the low one thousand range. Defenses that were once overwhelming were immediately out scaled in the course of one night. Whatever system is used to dictate the difficulty of monsters in relation to the size of corruption needs to be tweaked.

Despite my frustration with the corruption scaling, this game is still fun. Managing my village and defenses while beating back the corruption is an engaging challenge. I'm not sure if it's a difficulty thing, but the loot crate spawns felt way too high, being able to grab something like 20 of every piece of equipment from them sorta removes the urgency for smithing related buildings. 

I might edit this review later, pending another few runs.

review_text:
Another Metroidvania game, although this one is more of a Meroidvania-lite game. Unlike others it is shorter with smaller maps with less power-ups needed to collect everything, at most you'd just need to buy a spell or two in order to unlock certain things without much backtracking needed.

[b]Pros[/b]:

The pixel art and animation is beautiful. Everything just flows to well and doesn't really hide itself in the background. The most important animations look quite gorgeous with all that extra care given to them.

With it being metroidvania-lite the backtracking really is cut down, at most you barely have to go back to get other items be it for yourself or quest items for others. A lot of the times you just need to take the long way around or just need one certain spell.

A lot of different weapons and accessories to make your own build as the game goes on, able to change it up as you grab new stuff to see what you find the most fitting.

Beating the game once unlocks other game modes to spice up new playthroughs, all three of them varied in a way with one of them having a huge variance compared to the other two as it even has a bunch of new dialogue.

[b]Neutrals[/b]:

This depends more on how much you want to play this game, because it is short. One playthrough on average would take about two hours. Even 100%ing would not take that long if you don't idle, or do stupid things like me.

Quests are kinda forced upon you, along with returning the reward. Should you bump into the character that gave you the quest, you'll be forced to give up the item even if you wanted it. There's also one questline that's the same thing three times and it just begs the question of why. He isn't even that important of a character, he is just kinda there.

Combat first time around feels stiff, it takes time to adjust to it because your character swings it like they know how to fight, but don't have the stats to wield that weapon, and there is no leveling to fix this.

Story is.. there. It exists, it isn't terrible, but I could of had the same experience with the game if it didn't exist. I'd say just experience the dialogue once if you want since it isn't very long, otherwise just skip through.

[b]Cons[/b]:

Dodge rolling is pretty weak in this game, aside from a select few moments, it often just puts you in a tough spot. The enemy is either ready to attack again when you just get back up or you rolled too much and were too far away for a counterattack. A lot of the time it is better to just jump around the enemy to hit them.

Fighting enemies is pointless. This game has no leveling system and since only a few enemies have a guaranteed droprate of one item. The money they drop is pitiful and a lot of the loot they can drop is also pitiful. They can just drop nothing most of the time. So it is just better to not fight anything that isn't in the way or a boss.


Overall it was a pretty nice experience. Really enjoyed the different game modes, especially the big one. Though I hope the next game these guys work on improves the system when it comes to combat, at least giving some reason to fight the random enemies, Also this game has the best Mimic design I've seen in a good while.

review_text:
Actual game is pretty fun, but there are a few things that hold it back. Namely, sloppy parkour and an un-skippable "warmup" before the actual game starts, every time. By sloppy parkour, I mean that the player's speed is often useless against enemies. With enough practice, you can go extremely fast, but the enemies are unable to keep up. Meaning that a lot of the time, you wallrun into an arena, kill one or two enemies in the air, and then are forced to sluggishly jump around on the ground in order to deal with the rest. Ground movement speed is also far too low. I get that you go faster in the air, but the speed at which the player walks is honestly just anti-fun garbage atm. Combine that with less than accurate wallrunning detection, buggy monkey bars and speed boosts, and a bugged door that doesn't work half the time and you have the worst part of the game, "the void". A parkour tutorial is fine, but it should be reserved for a help menu or the tutorial already present. Having to do the same 3-4 parkour layouts every time you start a run is awful for everyone. It's too difficult (and buggy) for new players, and irritating for experienced ones. Half the time you'll spend 10 minutes on the parkour and then close the game because of how bad the hit detection is. It's also worth mentioning that the maps are not randomly generated. Despite being a roguelike, the game has set levels that you'll have to go through every single time you play it. Set levels + unskippable buggy parkour = not very replayable. I really, really want to like this game, but atm, it's far too sluggish and irritating to fully recommend.

TLDR: Gunplay is fun, game looks great, but the parkour and unskippable tutorials make the game sluggish and a chore to play. I truly believe that the game will become better if given enough time, though.
processed_text: actual game is pretty fun , but there are a few things that hold it back . namely , sloppy parkour and an un-skippable warmup before the actual game starts , every time . by sloppy parkour , i mean that the player ' s speed is often useless against enemies . with enough practice , you can go extremely fast , but the enemies are unable to keep up . meaning that a lot of the time , you wallrun into an arena , kill one or two enemies in the air , and then are forced to sluggishly jump around on the ground in order to deal with the rest . ground movement speed is also far too low . i get that you go faster in the air , but the speed at which the player walks is honestly just anti-fun garbage atm . combine that with less than accurate wallrunning detection , buggy monkey bars and speed boosts , and a bugged door that doesn ' t work half the time and you have the worst part of the game , the void . a parkour tutorial is fine , but it should be reserved for a help menu or the tutorial already present . having to do the same 3-4 parkour layouts every time you start a run is awful for everyone . it ' s too difficult ( and buggy ) for new players , and irritating for experienced ones . half the time you ' ll spend 10 minutes on the parkour and then close the game because of how bad the hit detection is . it ' s also worth mentioning that the maps are not randomly generated . despite being a roguelike , the game has set levels that you ' ll have to go through every single time you play it . set levels + unskippable buggy parkour = not very replayable . i really , really want to like this game , but atm , it ' s far too sluggish and irritating to fully recommend . tldr gunplay is fun , game looks great , but the parkour and unskippable tutorials make the game sluggish and a chore to play . i truly believe that the game will become better if given enough time , though .

review_text:
as a VR fps game BONELAB succeeds pretty well, the only criticism i have is that the weapon balancing is kind of strange. Only certain weapons kan one-shot in the head and deal even less damage to the body, resulting in you basically being able to mag-dump enemies and still barely killing them.
What sticks out are the mods however, i have played this game for longer than my steam hours on the oculus platform, and BONELAB becomes incredibly fun with mods, from better and more balanced guns(often having extra functions as well, such as customizable sights, stocks, etc) to avatars, the mods are what makes BONELAB stand out as a really fun VR gun experience, which i really recommed.

however the worst aspect of BONELAB is the games achivements. They are either so unclear to a point which i had to look up guides for several of them(which i wouldn't have done unless its achivements are as unclear as they are), and there are also a few examples of them not working at all. The achivement for beating Container Yard is techincally impossible right now due to a game bug(only obbtainable by basically forcing the game to remove a capsule from a place by aggressively ripping on it until its forcibly removed, which is supposed to be able to just grab and remove). there is also another achivement requiring you to throw a clipboard in a piece of lava (and as of the time of writing this review i have still not obtained it) and for whatever reason when i do so, it just doesnt give me the acheivement, im unsure if im doing something wrong or if its just my game that is bugged, but even excluding said achievement there are still several other aspects bugged.

so if you're looking for a really fun VR fps game to play alone(or with others, yes there is a multiplayer if you mod it), its really fun, and i HIGHLY recommend that you mod the game (its also really easy if you download it via mod.io ingame though cetain mods wont work as they need to be manually installed), but if you're planning on 100% the game, expect to be infuriated many times, both by the achievement requirements, but also the fact that the vanilla guns can be kind of annoying sometimes.

I really, really wanted to love this game, but throughout it's development from early access to it's official release, they just kept dropping the ball.

Every update is supposed to make the game more stable, but there always seems to be an issue even after the big 1.0. Whether that be someone lagging, dropping frames, the in-game servers crashing, the game itself just crashing, it continues to happen to someone at random in my friend group. If it is something like the in-game servers crashing, then it'll hit us all and kick us out the match. Do you get partial progress or XP after the game crashes in some way after an hour long match? No. Nothing. An hour or longer wasted on some of the more intensive operations and game modes.

The first thing I'm greeted with after the big update? DLC. 10 dollars a pop for a new color variation for your weapons, armor, helmet. Oh, and the only player card cosmetics that have been released that have come out with the 1.0 update? All in the DLC packs. If you played the game before in beta, the only thing you've really gotten is a weapon skin, and whatever progress you were able to make while playing and the game didn't crash.

The worst thing this update that killed any motivation to really continue playing? The new 'Company' system. Do you want to play with your friends in your own company, along with players you like/met and enjoyed playing during matches? Well fuck you. The only companies you can join are what we ~randomly~ recommend. Hope you and your friend rolled the same random search results and can join a stranger's company at least,  to progress through the 'story/battle pass' stuff together. No, you can't invite someone directly to your company. No, you cannot search for a specific company. How in the hell do you release this system which is supposed to be a major game play focus/mechanic in this state? I suppose if you are a solo player, then it doesn't matter that much.

This is all without mentioning some of the gripes about game itself. The environments can be a big hit or miss, the bugs can be very.. buggy, in the menus or in matches you can still encounter consistent bugs. I still have the 'new unlock' pop up since beta in my class stuff for a class I've already maxed, that has been here for over half a year. 

I want to love the game, the good parts of it are the gun play and game play loop does generally feel good. It has been fun to play with friends. Despite that, sadly no one in my friend group really wants to continue playing anymore after the bad experiences have outweighed the good thanks to the bugs, serving breaking, and instability. I fear for the game's long term health, for several reasons. I just can't recommend it.

review_text:
[b]Tldr[/b]
After almost 4 years and 100 levels of 'content', I would guess that dev team's core philosophy behind NGS is something along the lines of :

Put in the least amount of effort, recycle content wherever and whenever possible.

Not too concerned about growing the playerbase, the priority is to squeeze the tiny amount of players who have proven that they will tolerate the above and spend significantly and regularly on fashion items.

This is a game that's not very important to us or the company. We just keep the lights on and can continue operating like this for 100's of levels to come. The players will allow us. Most of the proceeds from NGS are invested into other projects.


[b]Level 100 Cap Update[/b]
Sadly, but not particularly surprisingly, most of the things from the old review are still true. I talk about the new stuff here, check the old review towards the end to see more about the game in general.

There still exist weapons with absurd drop rates, but as of lately the devs have been ensuring that there's a weapon option that the player can work towards and grind the materials for. If you play casually, the cost of gearing isn't painful. If you're min maxing, it's not as costly as it was before but the caveats and rng associated with successfully pulling it off still exist.
They story so far in almost 4 years and 100 levels remains lackluster (to put it generously) and is only able to accomplish anything remotely interesting when it key jangles characters from or links to the old game. The new Urgent Quest (equivalent to a raid in other mmo's) is a fight against the Level 100 cap update 'Final' Boss and that along with the scant amount of story, are the only content of what the devs consider a major update. [b]Everything else is recycled content, business as usual for NGS.[/b]

The fight itself leaves a lot to be desired and I wouldn't consider it befitting of a major story update boss. I've seen them design better fights for what would be considered less important bosses in the past few years. For major new raids, mmo devs would usually have an idea of how each class would perform in a fight..for example how Class A will position itself during this phase of the fight or the possible ways Class B might upkeep their damage during this particular attack from the boss. The NGS devs? Well, they do know, what I'm saying is they don't give a fuck. They can't be assed to craft an enjoyable, worthwhile 'final' boss experience for all their players. The content has been getting lazier and lazier and they're always testing how much they can keep recycling. 

I wanna point out that I'm calling this bitch a 'Final' boss according to the presented story beats and heavy implication that there won't be any significant story updates anytime soon, along with the fact that the credits play after as well. Frankly, I believe that they can and probably will go on well past 100 levels in their typical lazy, scripted and soulless fashion of delivering content.


[b]Slightly Older Review[/b]

I can write an essay on this, but I'll keep it brief. 
The two best and most outstanding qualities of this game are its combat and its fashion/character customization. Everything else..and I mean literally everything else about the game is severely lacking and objectively bad, so much so that its frustrating because the aforementioned is really, really good. 
The dev team is very rigid and stubborn and are excrustiatingly slow to balance and update things related to gameplay.

The combat and fashion as I said are the only things the game has going, but if you wanna get into either of them and enjoy them fully, it will require a lot of irl spending. The fashion items and fun emotes and stuff are buyable with ingame money, but the amount of that you will make as free to play would require you to do a mundane activity in game for 8+ hours to afford one, maybe two, items you might be interested in.

If you enjoy gearing and min maxing, then I highly recommend staying away from this game. There are certain weapon drops that are on the level of myths. There's a thing called Fixa which every weapon can have attached to it and it comes in 5 levels and different effect types. They only [b]recently[/b] made it so that the player can recreate this on a weapon that doesn't have it, either by spending a copious amount of free to play resources you accumlate over the course of several months..(for just a rng chance of getting it on one single weapon in the end) or by whaling on the game obscenely hard. Fixa has existed since the game's release and has always been a major point of contention, which took the devs 3 years to even begin to address.

The only way I could recommend this game is if you intend to play it casually on and off. It's arguably perfect for that and can easily be picked up and dropped. The combat is fun and you'll likely find a weapon and class you enjoy playing. All classes function as dps, so if you enjoy playing support in games you might not be as interested. Raids, bosses and whatever else have no real mmo mechanics that require any team oriented strategy..most of the game's strategy is found in optimizing your dps. 

That's about it..and yes, this was brief for how much could be said about the dev team dropping the ball so hard on a game with this much potential. They will never understand the extent to which they harmed and lost the community and following they had going with this franchise. 
Thanks for taking the time to read my review.

[Answer] TLDR;  No, don't download this game, UNLESS you need a good side game. Just play the more complete package of the base game if you wanted to have a taste of what NGS should have been. Legacy PS02 is an 8/10 while NGS is a 5/10 game. 


This is my in-depth review directed towards the "New Genesis" Game, not the legacy game hidden behind it. Steam state's that I played this game 4,6k+ hours, but in actuality I've clocked in double, heck even triple the amount of time since I played during the Microsoft launch BETA. 

:Pros:

- [Great graphics that can be further enhanced with re-shading and other third party methods.]

- [Combat controls are fluid and intuitive.]

- [Very easy to pick up mechanics regarding gear/leveling up.]

- [Variety of different Races to choose from Human, Newman, Deuman, Cast.] Doesn't matter now, race is "free-form" 

- [Game pacing is very quick, you can be gone for months and catch up fairly quickly.]

- [In-depth character creator with many facet's of customization that's arguably "one of the best" on the market.]

- [Fantastic Fashion for your player avatar]

- [Personal Quarters Customization is quite complex and actually really fun to play with.]

- [Space faring aesthetic] 

- [Makes a great "side game" If you can stomach existing along side the player-base.] Wow that's a pro?

:Cons:

- [Lacks meaningful content and poorly designed endgame.] Main content to this day is STILL PSE farming. Purple Triggers are boring once you subject yourself to artificially inflated difficulty that doesn't help you learn anything new to gain true mastery over anything except being "optimally perfect". Boss trigger content such as Dark Falz Aegis, Dark Falz ll, etc are well done, however still falls short due to being repetitive with bad reward structure. Enemy cannon fodder still feel like DPS sponges that take forever to kill making it feel like a really bad dynasty warriors game compared to base, despite having above average gear or hell even the best gear. Game doesn't respect your time. Not much else to say, let's move on.

- [Combat rewards are extremely unrewarding.] This one is a HUGE one for me. There is nothing more debilitating than watching last or current season's gear fall right into your inventory, only for it to be scrapped into a measily 80 meseta or however much it's worth. The only way for gear bit's to be worth any shread of Meseta, would be via Fixa's, but at that point you're just asking yourself if you want to slave away for copium drops. You can spend hours, days, weeks, even MONTHS, before you can even see something viable to even sell in the shop. The way I can see them fixing this, is by bringing back the system in base ps02, where you can exchange "useless" obsolete gear for things like ex-cubes, etc mats. I'd love to have some form of material progression, that won't require me to go out into the world shooting rocks all day like genshin impact.

- [Poor Story] The character's are easily forgotten. Poorly written dialogue that does not make any sense. Things just happen too fast, with little to no context or build up. If you're interested for the story alone, turn back. Many other games execute this better. There is nothing entertaining about these characters to make you care about them. The writing between base game and NGS is night and day.

- [Final con is the community.] I've been around for a very long time since base game in Japan to the beta of NGS. Traveled on 3 ships [Primary ship is 2], under different aliases. All of this is being said based on my own experiences, which is subjective to some if not most people. This game has some of the most mentally unhealthy/degenerate/heinous groups of people I've ever had the displeasure to be associated with. As with most anime games, it was going to be inevitable that such groups like this would exist within an MMO space. It's very hard to describe this community without stating the obvious facts. It's weird, horny, and you got some of the most mentally stunted adults I've ever seen in a video game period. 


Despite it's flaws, I love this game franchise to death as a long time fan and wish it nothing but success. It has SO much potential as an MMO and the proof shows with the previous iteration of the game despite the legacy game having it's own share of major problems that hindered it's development. However that is still no excuse for a game that was built on the ashes of that success only to heavily fall short. It sadden's me that I can't recommend this game to anyone. It's a badge of embarrassment and shame in it's current form. 

Phantasy Star, a franchise that was ahead of it's time that paved the way for other games to exist and be successful. SEGA should be ashamed of the legacy that is now stained. A lot of us waited 8 year's for the original MMO game to come to the west only for them to abandon it a year later to chase souless open world gaming trend with NGS. What a damn shame SEGA.

review_text:
This game just kind of sucks right now, despite its addictive quality.  The difficulty (especially on expert) is really front ended, in the sense that the first few teams you face have way more resources and abilities than the player does.  For example, the greasy lettuce should be a really easy team to face.  However, their speed and accuracy as well as their goalie is so far beyond what the player has that it's almost always a scripted loss.  It just leaves the player frustrated before ever getting to the later areas that offer more entertainment.   I can't count how many times I've lost while getting 30 shots, and they've only gotten 4 shots, but my goalie is so crappy that he let in two floaters from the blue line, and I lose 2-0.

The latter areas on the other hand are much more fun and test the player's skill as they navigate their way through some of the more hilarious abilities the teams have.  It's just that it's so rare to get to those levels.  I understand that the idea of the game is to get more entertaining as the player progresses, but it would greatly improve the quality if the first few games weren't so RNG dependent.  Seriously, fix the player's goalie.  That would improve the game greatly.

The good news is that this is an early access game, and most of these complaints are relatively easy fixes, so I would stay tuned for more development.

Edit after 0.1.6 update:  It still sucks.  They made it even harder to score.  You now have to pump all your stats into accuracy to have a prayer of scoring on hard mode, which of course leaves your speed and checking in the toilet.  This makes it impossible to stay with the other teams in the later levels.  So pick how you want to lose.  So it still feels like a middle finger to the player.

They made Butcher a little more reliable. So, in a way, it's more fair, in the sense that you won't lose to crappy goal tending quite so often.  But sense you can't score either, it doesn't matter.  It's just a more boring loss now.

Just prepare to lose on hard mode.

Devs... I should not lose 3-0 with 8-50 shot differential.  Now you're just screwin with us.

Update 4/19/2024:  Not much better.  Skill has no impact on likelihood of winning.  Just random chance.

It's fun... at first.

This game has a steep learning curve and it leaves a lot of questions for you to figure out on your own. It isn't very intuitive when it comes to understanding what you need to do to when there are problems. The UI is kind of clunky and difficult to work around, but I was able to fumble through it. After a few restarts, I thought that I had it figured out, but nope. Despite having farms with farmers , animals, chickens and a kitchen with cooks, my people start dropping like flies due to starvation. Is there a hunger strike programmed into the game or is it just that buggy? If it isn't the game then it would be nice to know what I'm supposed to do to force feed my citizens or why they chose to starve rather than eat the food that's right in front of their face. 

A game with such complexity needs an official manual. I found myself googling answers for the problems I was having and the steam forums are what turned up because many people were running into the same problems that I was having. Some solutions worked. Some didn't.

Maybe I'll give it another try sometime if the developer makes a play manual or wiki and fixes the AI. The sound and music are great, but being punished for no apparent reason after investing a few hours of game play isn't fun at all and that is why I cannot recommend this game. Currently, there seems to be more emphasis on ruining rather than rising. 

I see the developer likes to post negative reviews on twitter and then blame the player for not having fun in a condescending and bullying manner. Not very classy or professional Raymond. Also, 2+2=4 and that is a universally understood fact... because it is mathematics and not semantics or 1984 :) Good luck on your game and I hope you'll use the constructive criticism wisely instead of dismissing it

review_text:
Lost Ruins is a very simple and overall decent action platformer (not a metroidvania) . It is quite generic, feels overall quite solid, and its sprite work is probably the most standout thing about it. The difficulty is not crazy, and the game is easy to cheese, if that's what you want. I played the game for around 6 hours and nearly 100% completed it. If you're looking for something to play, get this on the cheap and it'll kill 6 hours—you could do far worse. 

[h1] Story & Presentation[/h1]
There isn't a whole lot to say about the story. It's not especially deep; the main playthrough has almost zero characterisation almost on any character—they're all quite bland. The premise is you've been summoned from another world and must kill *the things* in order to regain your memories and cue the highly predictable plot twist at the end. There are books scattered about for extra plot too, they're short and much like the story as a whole, don't outstay their welcome. 

In the post-game, a new mode unlocks that lets you play the story through in a different way, with some different characters that have actual personality. I have not finished this, but so far it is slightly more engaging?

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
The gameplay is quite solid, but overly simple to be truly satisfying or anything above "average." You have melee weapons and magic. You have weapons that stab, swing overhead, some that are slow, and some that are fast. Your magic options are spinny balls of ice, fire, electric, or a projectile of those elements. There are a couple more creative ones, like invisibility, absorbing corpses and the like for HP, but again, nothing that'll rock your socks off. 

A positive that the game has is that accessories, and some weapons, have unique effects which are quite impactful and can create many OP or cheese strategies. You won't find boring "+1" attack damage armour, for instance. It's usually +50% bleed, +30% extra damage against orcs, etc. While in some senses these are mundane, they're big increases you can exploit. Some are way more unique, such as getting +1 HP regeneration when wet, or +3 HP regeneration when bleeding, immunity to being frozen and etc. While these are just generic immunities and buffs, they're impactful and you can FEEL their impact on gameplay, which can't be said for every game these days. It makes your choice of accessories quite impactful, and there are a lot of synergies and builds you can go for. It's simple and a bit of fun.

Another thing I liked was the interaction between elements. The game has reactions between elements, such as water being hit with an ice spell will freeze it, doing damage to enemies in it (and yourself). Gasoline can catch fire and deal fire damage. The game even messes with you in places with this, putting jars of gasoline and candles you can accidentally destroy to light yourself on fire. It isn't a complex system, but, like everything else, it's simple and a bit of fun.

[h1] Exploration [/h1]
Lost Ruins has a metroidvania-looking map, but for the most part, it's a long linear corridor to the end. It has branching paths that will reward your exploration with unique accessories and weapons, as described above. There's a decent variety of biomes available as well. It keeps it from being too samey. There's a good mix of enemy types, although all of them are super simple and quite easy to kill overall. They look and feel very good to fight against.

[h1] Bosses & General Combat [/h1]
The bosses in this game have great sprite work and vibrant animations for the most part and feel very alive. Sadly, the complexity of the combat system and their attacks don't reach that same bar of quality, unfortunately. They'll have very few attacks, often 3-4 they'll cycle between, sometimes they'll also just de-aggro and stand in the arena doing nothing while you heal? It's unfortunate.

I played this game on the hardest difficulty available at the start. You take 50% more damage, and critical hits deal more damage to you as well (and statuses stack, like poison). This often meant you pretty much HAD to play perfectly a lot of the time and would go from full health to zero in seconds. Most of the time you lose reams of health in what feel like very unfair ways. You have no invincibility frames, so some attacks can just wombo combo you while you're stunned. If you survive on a sliver of health, good luck, because now you've got 4 stacks of bleed, all lasting 20+ seconds. You can open up the menu and eat all your cheese, cheese it if you will, and get full health again, but this doesn't feel very satisfying. Hard mode in this sense just feels brutally punishing, needing you to play to perfection. I presume normal mode isn't as bad and may even be a complete cake walk. The same that can be said here also applies to general enemy encounters. 

The beginning of the game was quite a bit more brutal as well, having low HP. Critical hits from enemies were the most annoying. Sometimes you just get one-shot from full HP if you get unlucky with an enemy crit. The game probably could have done without these, as it already punishes you enough for small mistakes, rather than getting run over by a crit from a red slime that does 21 damage out of your max 20 HP.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Overall, "it's simple and a bit of fun." sums the game up in a sentence. The quality of experience varies; it has some issues here and there, and it's a shame the boss designs don't have gameplay that matches their quality, but that doesn't make it bad or terrible, just mediocre and okay.

review_text:
I have mixed feelings about this game. First of all it's hardly a game, but more of a visual novel with minor interactive elements. The gameplay feels like an afterthought by the developers; very little effort was put in it. It's mostly just searching for the next trigger that advances the story, and couple of minigames here and there. It's tedious busywork that only gets in the way of enjoying the story. The player has no meaningful choices and there's no way to fail.

The controls are quite clunky. I played through the game using gamepad, which probably was a mistake. There's no way to reconfigure the movement buttons, and by default it uses the analog stick (instead of d-pad), which is awkward. And there are couple features in the game that don't work at all with gamepad, so I occasionally had to switch to mouse + keyboard.

The good thing about the game is its story. It's emotional and touching, and the beautiful soundtrack definitely helps that. There are some moments when the story touches on some pretty heavy subjects.

At the same time the whole thing feels a bit too sentimental. It overloads the player with emotional scenes, and there's always some melancholic music playing on the background. After a while it doesn't have the same impact anymore and by the time you get to the story's climax you just wanna see it all end as soon as possible.

review_text:
At the current price point its a waste of money. There is about 20€ worth of content in here and its not exactly all high quality content. For everything done right the game does something monumentally stupid. 
For example the game gives you a dodge to reveal enemy weak points, great idea solid way to reward accurate shooting. But then it binds said weakpoint mechanic to you having 100% stamina. So if you jumped, ran prior to battle or god forbid got hit a second ago that entire mechanic is effectively disabled. Worse yet weapons in this game have essentially 0 accuracy outside of scoped in mode so even when you reveal said weakpoint there is still a 50% chance to completely miss it because you did not scope in when shooting. 

Another example. [b]The game upgrades weapons and gear not just numerically but also via added special effects.[/b] So you get a challenge(kill x amount mostly) and then you can use a materials to boost your item. Neat idea that is completely invalidated by said upgrades being hidden from the player. Yes, you read that correctly. You are given no info on what the upgrade will do before you execute it, so you might easily waste an hour farming materials for an upgrade that in the the end you did not even want. 

Or how about this. [b]You have a limited amount of ammo and spells recharge very slowly so logically you need to plan your moves carefully ahead to not screw yourself. [/b] Great, I have to carefully choose my battles, except you cannot because the game will you just randomly spawn in enemies so you essentially cannot plan for shit because that one elite and five scrubs can easily spawn in additional two elites mid fight and even behind you so every encounter turns into effectively a coin toss as to whether you will be able to finish it. 

I could go on but I suppose my point is clear. The game is schizophrenic in its design. It does one thing and then undermines it for no gain whatsoever. It legitimately feels like half the design decisions were made to accommodate some future change or some cheese strategy that exists only on paper. 

Buy it on sale or avoid entirely.

-Raid mechanics, in depth and fun mechanics to keep boss fights interesting in the 10 man raids.

-Cosmetic costs, although all these items are purely cosmetic (so I will give some leniency) The cost for most cosmetics in this game is absolutely unhinged, for the nicest skins in the store it will run you right around $40, and with the current special draw doubling in price each "draw" it quickly becomes unreasonable for what should have been a $30-$40 outfit.

-AI voice acting, very distracting during some points in the game. I finally switched to Chinese voice actors (which are fantastic) but I understand that not everyone wants to have to read everything the characters are saying.

Overall I would highly recommend this game to just about every kind of player. I missed a lot of things in this review (both good and bad) but I hope I hit most of the high highs and the low lows. To me this game is a MUST PLAY.

Buying any game in early access is a risk, but sometimes your investment pays off. Once this game is finished it'll be better, right now it's good but there's only 3 arenas, limited enemies and gear. Yet within the limitations of this game there's still items that don't have a purpose somehow. Looking at you black salt.

Gameplay wise there's a lot of times when you are doing multiple encounters at once, and with the enemies wandering off it can lead to completely unfair encounters that weren't intended to be fought the way they are presented, while doable it's pretty annoying having 6 swordsmen who can teleport and become invincible just be on top of you. Although I will say, sound design and art design are great they did a good job on the gun sounds.

review_text:
I bought the Gold Edition of this game after being blown away by its spectacular trailer and stunning artwork. Unfortunately, I fell for the classic case of judging a book by its cover — and ended up paying full price for it. Once launched, it became clear that the trailer was heavily pre-rendered and not representative of the actual gameplay. The graphics feel outdated, comparable to games from 2011, despite the game being quite demanding on system resources.

The combat mechanics show some promise but are ultimately underdeveloped, clunky, and uninspired. Most battles take place during sieges, and the combat system lacks proper support for fighting multiple enemies at once, which quickly becomes frustrating. The game is divided into two acts: the first is engaging and encourages you to keep playing. The second act, though larger in scale, feels empty and dull. Continuing beyond Act One felt more like a chore, and it's clear the developers cut corners toward the end. What a shame.

I wouldn’t recommend buying this game at full price. It feels highly unfinished and lacking in proper development. If you're curious, wait for a sale—and definitely skip the Gold Edition. Even after finishing the main story, I couldn’t bring myself to complete the DLC. It’s just plain boring.

It's cruel, disgusting, disturbing yet beautiful. 
The creatures look like they've emerged from the sock under my bed, trying to survive, and you're just there, letting the atmosphere sink in and fighting for your life... If it looks like something you'd enjoy, pick it up. It aims for a very specific feel and nails it. However, not everyone will be fond of that feel. 

For completionists: you get all achievements for just playing the game, then the last achievement, for replaying the first segment and doing something a bit differently. Expect around 5-6 hours of playtime.

There is one thing that bothers me though: The lack of multiple endings. Given the choice at the beginning, the lack of multiple endings really does sting, since the ending does make it seem like there could be a better outcome, and I'd love to see that outcome, but the game just doesn't give it to you.

review_text:
I've got hundreds of hours in Titanfall, Trepang2 and Ultrakill. I'm not new to movement shooters whatsoever. But there is something rubbing me the wrong way about this game, and I think it comes down to enemies, level design and the loot aspect, I'll address each below.

ENEMIES: I think it's pretty unfair how the spawning and movement of them work. you can't predict where they'll be, where they're going or when they spawn making me flip and shoot at random most of the time instead of moving strategically it just becomes a Parkinson simulator. I think them teleporting is a cheap way to make them feel like they're keeping up with me and it's led to me whiffing shots or getting jumped on at random times. They hit like a truck which would be fine if 1. they didn't just matterialize out of nowhere and 2. did have instant hit frames the second they spawn or teleport. Why not have wall running enemies or just have them jump gaps so I can at least have a chance to hit them mid air or see where they're going.

LEVEL DESIGN: The wall running is clunky at best, I've toyed around with the setting and nothing feels right or good. you either stick or you don't, and even then I've had multiple times where I stick to a wall and lose all speed and slide down. Not to mention you're VERY limited on walls that can be used as launch pads since everything in the game is shaped like a non-Euclidian surface. Too many things knock you out of a flow like weird jagged walls, tree roots for some reason and random steps on the floor. I can only imagine this is to slow you down so you don't outrun the AI too much.

LOOT
Good luck finding health like, ever. It was VERY rare I ever gained any health and if I did it was almost nothing. The economy seems a little one sided since I can't hand pick guns I have to gamble and the vending machine is finite? Just felt like there wasn't enough to risk experimenting with guns since I was gambling a large portion of my funds and I didn't have ways to keep trying without risking ANOTHER finite resource which I get it's part of the difficulty, but if I'm fighting the mechanics I really don't wanting to be getting spit roasted by the economy too. 

The guns felt GREAT and the animations were good, though I noticed at least three had no animation sound effects which felt awkward. I'm going to give this another chance tomorrow and see if I'm just having a bad day, but I'm debating uninstalling it. I'll keep up on the updates because I want this to succeed, it could be really fun in time, but there are better options out there

review_text:
PSO2 and PSO2:NGS, I can say after first starting in the Japanese Server during the launch of Episode 4. I started out alone and with no prior knowledge going into the game. The game itself does what it offers, a vast customization system, flashy but a bit janky combat, expansive skill trees (that you now have to pay AC and SG to fix in the classic version, but completely free in NGS), and a wide array of players from across the global.

The classic version first is very unforgiving if you're a new player as many events and handouts are no longer existing. With most players being veterans who've already completed the game and the final quest HTPD (The Primordial Darkness Hard Mode), Masquerade depth 999, and the time attacks of Rondo to flex with each other on. However on the NGS side you can jump right in and pick up and put down at your leisure. The story will carry you throughout the early progression as you get handouts and things to help you along the way.

Towards the Starless first part quest is when everything in NGS has to offer for you is fully unlocked, so you can skip the remainder of the lackluster story if you want to jump right in to the "endgame". For F2Ps there are things like dailies, weeklies, dext farming, and alnothe farming to be your main source of N-Meseta. However dext farming requires a more specific set up to min/max in which in a good group or a private farm you make 1.5m-2m meseta per hour spent (with either meseta boosters or 100% Rare Drop Boosters + 1 Hour Auto Sell Passes as the drops there adds up to your meseta count when auto-sold.)

I will be real with you though, with the game pushed from the ESRB to T to M, there has always been a slew of extremely lewd and cursed players who are unhinged and ERP in the local town hubs. Central City being the main criminal for that. People can be either toxic or cringe depending on how you approach them, but there are always a good bunch around. Making friends and connections will do you wonders in the game, both Classic and NGS.

Though the game loop is lackluster at best, having friends and making small and big goals helps you continue to want to play this game. I myself have spent 12k hours into this game, yet still find enjoyment despite I am beyond burnt out, fed up with the toxicity and lewdity, and have completed most major content in the game including HTPD in Classic. Would I recommend this game I would say both "yes" and "no". Yes, if you are the fashionista who loves cosplay, looking cute or cool or both, taking screenies with friends, alliances, or yourself, or don't have much time to grind so to do dailies and weeklies then scoot off. No because the game though not completely finished in NGS is brutal when it comes to gearing. As most things boils down to overly expensive augments, preset abilities, and expensive upgrading. Being a loner type will only get you so far as you'll be limited to solo only content or try-harding to the point you drop grands on the game.

My TL;DR if you do decide to play, find your niche, make friends, make a cool unique avatar, and just be yourself. It's both the game I love and hate, and could have been potentially one of the best Anime MMORPGs of its time. But because of sega's greed, monetization, and poor management, the game falls short of what made Phantasy Star, Phantasy Star.

Don't let my short playtime on Steam fool you, I've easily put at least 3000 hours into this game in the nearly 20 years it's been out, since I was a kid.

Roller Coaster Tycoon 2 is far from the perfect simulation game.  Hell, it isn't even the perfect tycoon game, but it's okay because I guarantee it wouldn't have been nearly as engrossing of a game if it was.

Have you ever wanted to recreate your favorite real life parks using an incredibly feature-rich scenario editor?
RCT2 has it.
Ever wanted to spend hours fine tuning the perfect roller coaster only to realize you don't have the money to actually build it so you give in to the rapidly approaching neurosis that ultimately gives way to an extreme mental breakdown?
RCT2 has it.
Have you ever wanted to recreate meme rides like Mr. Bones' Wild Ride, the Fiery Fist O' Pain, or 𝑀𝒾𝒸𝓀𝑒𝓎'𝓈 𝒟𝒾𝒸𝓀 𝒮𝓂𝒶𝓈𝒽𝑒𝓇?
